# SOURCE: content_invoice_extraction_v1.109.md
---

# Content Invoice — Extraction Logic
**Version:** 1.110
**Model Target:** claude-sonnet-5-5
**Min Token Estimate:** ~10,600
**Cache Strategy:** explicit
**Last Updated:** 2026-09-23

---

## Purpose

Extracts structured data from vendor Content/Delivery Invoices submitted to EspriGas. These invoices bill EspriGas (as reseller/bill-to) for gas cylinder fills and associated fees delivered to an end-customer (ship-to) location. EspriGas's company address is 3007 Earl Rudder Fwy S, Suite 500, College Station TX 77845.

**Key identifiers for this document type:** Header says `"INVOICE"` or `"ORIGINAL INVOICE"`. Line items include gas cylinder products and fee lines (DELIVERY, FUEL, HAZMAT). Does NOT have a "CYLINDER RENTAL INVOICE" header or rental group columns.

**Multi-document / Mixed PDF handling:** A single PDF file may contain multiple distinct documents — either different document types across pages, or multiple documents of the same type. Treat each distinct document independently:
- Classify each page independently. If a page is identified as a Rental Invoice, route it to the Rental Invoice extractor.
- When a PDF contains multiple invoices of the same type (e.g., two content invoices), produce a separate extraction output for each.

**Credit Memo routing:** Before applying any content invoice extraction rules, check for credit memo signals. If the invoice total is negative, carries a `CR` suffix (e.g., `151.91 CR`), or the document header or a label directly above the line items contains `"CREDIT MEMO"`, `"CREDIT NOTE"`, or `"CREDIT INVOICE"`, reclassify as a Credit Memo and route to `credit_memo_extraction.md`. Do not extract as a Content Invoice.

**Mixed Invoice routing:** Classification as a Content Invoice is provisional until line-level inspection is complete (GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §7.6). If both Content lines and Rental lines are found within a single invoice number on this document, reclassify as a Mixed Invoice and route to `mixed_invoice_extraction.md` instead. Do not split or process the document here.

---

## Rental vs. Content Classification

Use the following signals to determine whether a page is a **Rental Invoice** rather than a Content Invoice. Check all patterns case-insensitively.

| Signal Type | Text / Field Value | Vendors |
|-------------|-------------------|---------|
| `"cylinder rental invoice"` in page text | Raw text | LAMPTON, SIDNEYLEE, GEERGAS, JACKSONWEL, VERNLEWIS, MCKINNEY, STARWELD, WELDSERVICE, MINNEAPOLIS, LOUISINA, WESTCOOP, UNITEDWELDING, NEARUCO2, ATLAS, PACIFICWELD, SYOXSA, AIRGASNATIONAL, IRISHCARBONIC, MAINOXY, AIRWELD, AWISCOCORP, DMI, JONESWELDING, AIRSUPPLY, HELGET, CWSUPPLY |
| `"cylinder"` AND `"rental"` both present | Raw text | HOLSTON |
| `"rental invoice"` in page text | Raw text | BECKLEYRENT, SKYOXYGEN, JMGASES |
| `"rent days"` in page text | Raw text | COASTALCARB, ROCKYMOUNT, AWI |
| `"monthly rental"` in page text | Raw text | ANALGESIC, MAVERICK |
| `"rental"` anywhere in page text | Raw text | ADVANCEDGAS, DELILLE, JMCYLINDER, SJSMITH, CESCO (uses `"telemetry"` instead) |
| PO Number field = `"RENTAL"` | Header field | SOUTHEASTERN |
| PO Number field = `"MONTHLY EQ"` | Header field | PREMIERMEDL |
| Comment/Route field = `"RENT"` | Header field | MAVERICK, UNITEDWELDING |
| Route/descriptor = `"Rent"` (capitalized) | Header field | AMERIGAS, PHILADELPHIA |
| Route/descriptor = `"cylinder rental"` | Header field | GENERALAIR |
| Route/descriptor = `"rental detail and description"` | Header field | PRAXLINDT |
| `"group bill"` in page header text AND `"O2TANKRENTAL"` item code in section lines | Raw text | NUCARA |

**NuCara Group Bill routing note:** A NuCara "Group Bill" PDF contains both rental and content invoice sections on the same pages. Route individual invoice sections based on line item codes: sections with `O2TANKRENTAL` → rent_invoice extractor; sections with `O2 E CONTENTS` or `DELIVERY CHARGE` → this extractor (content_invoice). See NuCara vendor section in Vendor Reference for full rules.

**Default:** If none of the above match and the page shows product lines with quantities and prices, classify as Content Invoice.

---

## Extraction Rules

### Bill-To vs. Ship-To

`customer_name` and `customer_address` always refer to the Ship-To (end customer location). `supplier_account_no` is EspriGas's account with the vendor. For EspriGas entity identification and the Ship-To Exclusion Rule, see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §1. **When the document prints more than the usual two address blocks** (e.g., a top-row `SHIP FROM` next to a `BILL TO`, or a bottom-row `BILL TO` next to the `SHIP TO`), extract all of them per GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §26 — do not discard the extras.

### Header Fields

| Field | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `partner_name` | Vendor/supplier name as printed on the invoice. **CSV/flat-file input with no vendor-name column: apply §3.11** — use the same value resolved for `trade_partner` below, instead of leaving this Tier 1 field absent. |
| `supplier_account_no` | EspriGas's account with the vendor. When a dedicated account number field is present in the invoice header, use it. When no dedicated header account field is present but the invoice separately prints a **Sold To Account No.** and a **Ship To Account No.**, prefer the **Ship To Account No.** unless a vendor-specific rule states otherwise. |
| `supplier_name` / `supplier_address` | The vendor's remit-to entity name and address — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §19. Omit both entirely when neither a remit-to block nor a general vendor address appears on the document. |
| `ship_from_name` / `ship_from_address` | The vendor's shipping-origin branch/warehouse, from a `SHIP FROM` block (typically paired with a top-row `BILL TO`) — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §26. Omit both entirely when no `SHIP FROM` block appears on the document. |
| `bill_to_name` / `bill_to_address` | The billed customer's (EspriGas's) name and address, from a `BILL TO` block — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §26. Omit both entirely when no such block appears on the document. |
| `invoice_no` | Vendor-assigned invoice number |
| `invoice_date` | Date on the invoice header |
| `invoice_total` | Total dollar amount |
| `terms` | Payment terms, normalized. Labels vary: `TERMS`, `PAYMENT TERMS`, `NET TERMS`. Normalize numeric day terms by stripping `DAYS`/`DAY` and prepending `NET ` (e.g., `45 DAYS` → `NET 45`, `NET 30 DAYS` → `NET 30`). Keep as-is: `COD`, `DUE ON RECEIPT`, `PREPAID`, `EOM`. Leave blank if absent. |
| `due_date` | Invoice due date. Extract directly if stated on document. Otherwise calculate from `invoice_date` + net days (parsed from normalized `terms`). For `COD`, `DUE ON RECEIPT`, `PREPAID`: use `invoice_date`. Leave blank if terms are absent or non-calculable. |
| `customer_name` | Ship-To name (end customer location) |
| `customer_address` | Ship-To address — split into `address_1`, `address_2`, `city`, `state`, `zip` |
| `buyer_code` | Vendor-printed code for the buying entity, branch, or division. Labels vary: `BUYER CODE`, `BRANCH`, `DIVISION`, `DEPT`, `SOLD-TO CODE`. **Do not restate `supplier_account_no` here** — if the only account-like code on the document is already captured there, output `""`. Always present in output; empty string when absent. No confidence deduction. See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §25. |
| `shipto_code` | Vendor-printed code for the ship-to location. Labels vary: `SHIP-TO CODE`, `SHIP TO NO.`, `LOCATION`, `SITE`, `STORE`, `ROUTE`, `WAREHOUSE`, `SHIP TO ACCT #`. When separate Bill-To and Ship-To account numbers are printed, the ship-to value goes here. **Do not restate `supplier_account_no`.** Always present in output; empty string when absent. No confidence deduction. See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §25. |
| `delivery_note_no` | Vendor's delivery note / delivery number. Labels vary: `DELIVERY NOTE No.`, `DELIVERY NOTE #`, `DELIVERY No.`, `DELIVERY TICKET No.`, `DEL NOTE`. Distinct from `order_no` and from the `tracking_number` parcel-tracking number. **Omit entirely when the label is absent** — no deduction. See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §24. |
| `bill_of_lading_no` | Vendor's bill of lading number. Labels vary: `BILL OF LADING NO.`, `BILL OF LADING #`, `B/L NO.`, `BOL`. **Keep separate from `delivery_note_no` even when both labels print the same value** — that is expected, not a duplication error. **Omit entirely when the label is absent** — no deduction. See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §24. |
| `trade_partner` | **CSV/flat-file input: check §3.10 first** — if the file has a `TradePartner` column, use its value directly (Priority 1); else if the filename carries a `<TradePartner>_` prefix, use that value directly (Priority 2); either way, do not run the lookup below. Otherwise: BC trade partner code for the supplier. Look up `partner_name` (case-insensitive) in the Trade Partner Reference table (§TP.2). If found and not listed in §TP.1, use the mapped code. If listed in §TP.1, output `INSTANTLRN` and flag per §TP rules. If no match found, output `INSTANTLRN`. |
| `customer_po_number` | End-customer's PO number. Labels vary: `CUS P/O #`, `CUSTOMER PO`, `PO NUMBER`, `PO #`, `CUST PO`. **If the document prints two separate PO fields** (e.g., `Hardgoods PO #` and `Gas PO #`), do not leave this blank just because neither label matches the list above — apply the Multi-PO Priority rule (Extended Extraction Rules, below) to resolve a single value. Leave blank only when no PO field of any kind is present on the document. Apply §13.10 BC PO number normalization after extraction. |
| `po_date` | Date of the customer PO. Per §15.3a, always prefer an explicitly-stated header field — do not substitute a value derived from a data column (e.g., MMDD from a SHIPPING ORDER column) when a header date field is present. Labels vary: `PO DATE`, `P/O DATE`, `ORD DATE`, `ORDER DATE`. **Default chain when absent from header:** `ship_date` → `delivery_date` (if separately stated) → `invoice_date`. Always populated in output. |
| `order_no` | Vendor's internal order/shipping order number. Labels vary: `ORDER #`, `ORDER NUMBER`, `SHIPPING ORDER NUMBER`, `SO #`. Leave blank if absent. |
| `ship_date` | Ship date if explicitly labeled on the document (SHIP DATE, SHIPPED, etc.). If absent from the header, apply in priority order: (1) check the line item table for a date column or date-encoded item column (§15.5a) and use that value; (2) use `delivery_date` if separately stated on the document; (3) fall back to the order/PO date (§15.5); (4) default `ship_date = invoice_date`. Always populated in output. For multi-delivery invoices, apply the same priority chain per delivery — use the ship date specific to that delivery if available (e.g., from the table); fall back to that delivery's delivery date only if no ship date is present. |
| `delivery_date` | Date product was delivered. Extract from document if present. **Fallback:** use the same value as `ship_date` (which may itself have been derived from a table date per §15.5a or an order/PO date per §15.5) → `invoice_date`. Always populated in output. |
| `ship_via` | Delivery method. Labels vary: `SHIP VIA`, `SHIPPED VIA`, `VIA`. Leave blank if absent. |
| `tracking_number` | Carrier shipment tracking number (UPS, FedEx, etc.), when printed on the document. Labels vary: `TRACKING #`, `TRACKING NUMBER`, `TRACKING`. **Strip the label itself — output only the `#` and the tracking code that follows it** (e.g., `TRACKING #1Z5WW0320335636545` → `#1Z5WW0320335636545`). If no `#` is printed before the code, output the code alone with no leading `#`. May appear in the invoice footer, a separate annotation area, or on a following page rather than in the main header block — check the full document, not just the header. **Omit this field entirely when not present on the document** — do not default to an empty string. Only a subset of vendors print this value; see vendor-specific notes (e.g., Southeastern Medical Equipment) below. Distinct from `comment` (GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §28) — a `TRACKING #` label is never a `Comment:` label. |
| `comment` | Text following a literal `Comment:` label anywhere on the document. See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §28 for the full extraction rule. **Omit entirely when no `Comment:` label is present.** |
| `is_rush` | Boolean — `true` when the document shows an expedite signal anywhere. **Scan three places, not just the header** (GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §23.2): (1) **line items** — any line resolving to `910019` Rush Delivery, or `RUSH`/`EXPEDITE`/`EXPEDITED` in a line's `item_no`/`description`; (2) **the line-item table region** — rush wording in a stamp, banner row, marginal annotation, or free text printed among the rows but belonging to no line; (3) **header fields** — `RUSH`/`EXPEDITE`/`HOT SHOT`/`STAT` in `ship_via`, order type, route, comments, notes. Single document-level value, not per-line. **Never create a line item from table-region annotation text**, and never alter a rush line that was read as a signal. **Excluded:** `910061` `Delivery Same Day Emergency Room` is a delivery destination, not an expedite — it never sets this flag. Output unquoted `true`/`false`. Always populated. No confidence deduction. |
| `delivered_by` | Carrier or delivering party, **UPPERCASED**, drawn in priority order from `ship_via` → route → an explicit `DELIVERED BY`/`CARRIER`/`DRIVER` field (GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §23.3). Distinct from `ship_via`, which stays as printed — populate both independently. **Omit entirely when no carrier is named** — no deduction. |
| `content_type` | Short-form record type — **derived from `document_type`, never read from the document** (GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §20). `content_invoice` → `Content`; `propane_invoice` → `Propane`. Always populated. No confidence deduction. |
| `care_of` | Intermediary/forwarding party from the Sold-To / Bill-To / Ship-To block, identified by a `C/O`, `C/O:`, or `CARE OF` marker. **Two strips, in order:** (1) remove the marker; (2) remove any EspriGas/TMG identifier and its adjoining delimiter, keeping everything that remains — e.g. `C/O ESPRIGAS CCBCC` → `CCBCC`. **Never output a bare EspriGas/TMG identifier**; if nothing remains after stripping, omit the field. Do **not** also write this line into `customer_address.address_2`, and do **not** use it as `customer_name`. A care-of line naming EspriGas/TMG does not trigger the §1 Ship-To Exclusion Rule. `ATTN`/`ATTENTION` lines are not care-of lines. **Omit entirely when absent** — no deduction. See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §21. |
| `additional_header_fields` | Any other labeled header field printed on the document that isn't captured by a field above — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §27. **Omit entirely when none found** — no confidence deduction. |

### Delivery Attributes

`is_rush` and `delivered_by` are defined centrally because they are shared across document types. **See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §23** for the `is_rush` signal list (§23.2), `delivered_by` extraction and normalization (§23.3), and the per-document-type applicability matrix (§23.4). Both apply to content invoices and propane invoices.

> **`delivery_type` and `is_will_call` were removed 2026-09-23** — no longer extracted, derived, or scored. Do not populate either field.
>
> **`is_rush` is not header-only.** Rush indicators appear on line items (notably a `910019` Rush Delivery fee line) and as free-floating text in the line-item table region — stamps, banner rows, marginal annotations. All three sources feed the one document-level flag; see §23.2 for the full ordered signal list and exclusions.

### Content Invoice Line Fields

| Field | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `item_no` | Vendor item/product code |
| `description` | Product description |
| `qty` | Quantity shipped |
| `unit` | Unit of measure. **Normalize to `"EA"` for all lines** regardless of what is printed on the document (`CYL`, `EACH`, blank, etc.) — **except bulk gas product lines** (billed by volume/weight — `GAL`, `GALLON`, `LB`, `LBS` — see Bulk Gas Product Lines below), which output their printed unit as-is. This normalization is a final output step; it does not change how `qty_returned` or any other field is determined (see below — the as-printed UOM may still inform vendor-specific rules before this normalization is applied). |
| `unit_price` | Price per unit |
| `line_amount` | Extended amount (Qty × Unit Price) |
| `qty_ordered` | Ordered quantity as explicitly stated in a dedicated column on the invoice. **Omit this field entirely when the vendor does not provide an ordered quantity column** — do not default to `0`. Only a subset of vendors print this value. Extraction rules to be defined when sample documents are reviewed. **PLACEHOLDER — RULES PENDING vendor document review.** |
| `qty_shipped` | Quantity of cylinders shipped. Output as `0` for fee/charge lines and any line with no shipment activity. **If `qty > 0` and `qty_shipped` is not present on the document, default `qty_shipped = qty`.** Never null or omitted. |
| `qty_shipped_provenance` | How `qty_shipped` was determined — never null or omitted:<br>• `"stated"` — read directly from a document column.<br>• `"defaulted"` — no shipped-quantity column/value on the document; set to `qty` per the fallback above.<br>• `"not_applicable"` — fee/charge line or line with no shipment activity; `0` is correct by rule, not a document reading. |
| `qty_returned` | Quantity of cylinders returned. Rules by line type — never null or omitted:<br>• **Bulk gas lines** (sold by volume/weight — LBS, GAL, MCF, CF, etc.): always `0`; set `qty_returned_provenance = "not_applicable"`.<br>• **Hardgoods purchase lines** (outright sales of any physical item — cylinders, regulators, valves, equipment, or any non-gas-exchange item): always `0`; set `qty_returned_provenance = "not_applicable"`. Do not apply the even-exchange assumption or deduction. **Do not use UOM as a signal here** — printed UOM is not a reliable purchase-vs-exchange indicator on its own (e.g., `CYL` is the standard exchange unit for most vendors, and the `unit` output field is normalized to `EA` regardless — see `unit` above). Identify a purchase line from: description contains `"SALE"`, `"PURCHASE"`, `"REPLACEMENT"`, or equipment-related terms; a dedicated purchase/sale indicator column; or an explicit vendor-specific rule (e.g., Tech-Gas — see Extended Extraction Rules — which may reference the document's as-printed UOM as part of that vendor's own known format, prior to the `unit` normalization above).<br>• **Cylinder lines — value present on document**: extract directly; set `qty_returned_provenance = "stated"`. Do NOT apply the even-exchange assumption — this line does not contribute to the "Assumed even exchange" flag or deduction, regardless of whether the extracted value happens to equal `qty_shipped`.<br>• **Cylinder lines — value absent or unable to be extracted**: default `qty_returned = qty_shipped` (even exchange assumed); set `qty_returned_provenance = "defaulted"`. **Do not add a flag or deduction on this line itself** — see the document-level "Assumed even exchange" check in Confidence Scoring below, which applies a single flat deduction once per document (not per line) when any line on the document is defaulted. |
| `qty_returned_provenance` | How `qty_returned` was determined — see rules above. One of `"stated"`, `"defaulted"`, `"not_applicable"`. Never null or omitted. Confidence scoring reads this field directly rather than inferring provenance from comparing `qty_returned` to `qty_shipped` — see Minor Flags below. |
| `esprigas_item_no` | Always written as an empty string (`""`) — placeholder, not resolved by Rosetta — see "`esprigas_item_no` — Always Empty" below. |

**Quantity field zero rule:** All quantity fields (`qty`, `qty_shipped`, `qty_returned`) must always be output as a number. When a quantity is zero, not applicable, or inferred to be zero, output `0` — never `null`, never omit the field. The `_provenance` companion fields are strings (not quantities) and are exempt from this rule — they follow their own three-value enum instead.

**Item Number Normalization:** After extraction by any method, apply the full normalization pipeline — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §13.3. ChangeAbbreviation and space removal (§13.3 Steps 1–2) are unconditional and always run first, regardless of whether any content-specific step below applies. The content-specific steps (prefix stripping, rental -R append, content hyphen rule) and truncation are in the Extended Extraction Rules — Item_No Transformations section below.

**Mixed Invoice — Rental Line Detection:** Some invoices contain both content and rental line items on the same page. Identify a line as a rental item (case-insensitive) when its description contains any of: `"RENTAL"`, `"RENT DAYS"`, `"MONTHLY RENTAL"`, or `"CYLINDER RENTAL"`. Append `-R` only to those lines. Content product lines and fee/charge lines are not affected. For identified rental lines, `qty_returned` is always zero — do not extract a return quantity for rental items.

**Typical content invoice line categories:**
- Gas cylinder fills (product lines): `ACT-MC10`, `MOXE`, `MOXK`, `MAIKH`, `MCDE`, `MLO230`, etc.
- Delivery fee: `DELIVERY` ($12.00) or `FEEDELIVERY` (varies)
- Fuel surcharge: `FUELSURCHARGE` or `FEEFUEL` (varies)
- Hazmat fee: `COMPLIANCEFEE` or `FEEHAZMAT` (varies)
- Maintenance: `HYDROTESTMAINTENANCE` ($14.50/ea), `ACETREQUAL` ($25.00/ea)
- Warranty: may appear at $0.00 (e.g., WARRANTY on HS 15354)

### Zero-Dollar Line Filtering

**General rule:** Exclude a line when ALL of the following are true:
- `qty_shipped = 0` — no cylinders shipped
- `qty_returned = 0` — no cylinders returned
- `line_amount = 0.00` OR `unit_price = 0.00` — not billed or rate is zero

This covers two patterns: lines with no activity at all (all qty fields zero, $0 amount) and fee/surcharge lines that carry a non-zero `qty` but were not applied ($0 unit price or $0 amount, no cylinder movement).

**Always include despite meeting the above:**

| Condition | Reason |
|-----------|--------|
| `qty > 0` AND line is a gas or product line (cylinder fill, bulk gas, medical gas — not a fee, surcharge, or charge) | Non-zero product quantity may represent demand charge billing or delivery captured elsewhere |
| `qty_returned > 0` | Cylinder return with no charge — must be tracked |
| Vern Lewis — item_no = `WARRANTY` | Real warranty record; $0.00 and zero qty are correct |
| Jackson Welding — DEL or Truck Charge lines | Delivery bundled in cylinder price; $0.00 and zero qty are expected |

> **PLACEHOLDER — EXCEPTIONS REVIEW PENDING:** Certain vendors or billing structures may produce $0.00 fee/surcharge lines that should be retained (e.g., contractually required line items that carry no charge, informational billing codes, or vendor-specific formatting). Add vendor-specific exceptions to the table above as they are identified.

> **General Air — Vendor Override:** For General Air (GENERALAIR) content invoices only, exclude any line where `unit_price = 0.00` **and** `line_amount = 0.00`, regardless of `qty_shipped`, `qty_returned`, or line type. This takes precedence over the general rule and its always-include exceptions above (including the `qty_returned > 0` exception) for this vendor only. See Vendor Reference — General Air Service & Supply.

**Non-Billable Annotation Rows — applies to any supplier.** Some invoice formats print a standalone row that visually resembles a line item — text in the Item/Description position, a number somewhere in the row — but is actually a restatement of activity already captured on a real product line above it, or a running-total annotation (e.g. a bare `"Cylinder Return"` row, a `"Cylinder Shipped Total:"` / `"Cylinder Returned Total:"` footer). These carry no `unit_price` or `line_amount` of their own, and any count printed on them typically belongs to a column this reference doesn't map to `qty`, `qty_shipped`, or `qty_returned` at all (an invoiced-unit count, a backorder count, a running tally) — **never** a reason for §13.4/Zero-Dollar Line Filtering to treat the row as having a real non-zero quantity. Before excluding or retaining a $0.00-looking row, confirm every number on it actually maps to a documented schema field per that vendor's column mapping; a number in an unmapped column can never satisfy the `qty > 0` or `qty_returned > 0` always-include exceptions above. When a row is confirmed to be this kind of annotation, discard it — do not create a line item from it, regardless of vendor. See `Indiana Oxygen Co. (INDIANAOXY)` — "PDF Format" below for a documented example of this exact pattern.

### Late Fee Line Items

When a content invoice contains one or more line items that are a late fee, past-due charge, or interest/financing charge (identified by description containing `"LATE FEE"`, `"LATE CHARGE"`, `"LATE PAYMENT"`, `"PAST DUE"`, `"FINANCE CHARGE"`, or `"INTEREST CHARGE"`, case-insensitive):

1. **Include the line** in the extracted output as normal.
2. Add flag `"(-10) late_fee_line — flagged for manual review"` to `confidence.flags`.
3. Deduct **−10** from confidence score per affected line.

> **Post-processing note — REVIEW PENDING:** A future option under consideration is to remove late fee lines entirely and reduce `invoice_total` by the corresponding `line_amount` before BC import.

### Email / Communication Page Detection

Skip pages that are email forwarding headers. When a page contains all three of `"from"`, `"to"`, and `"sent"` in close proximity, treat the page as non-extractable and move to the next page.

**Exception — never skip for:** SJSMITH, MESSER, CARBONICSERVICES, and invoice number `079056347`.

### Environment / Compliance Fee Lines

Lines where the description contains both `"ENVIRONMENT"` and `"COMPLI"`:
- Set `item_no = "ENV"`
- If both `line_amount` and `unit_price` are present and numeric: `qty = line_amount ÷ unit_price`
- If a separate "totals" computation row exists for the same fee, remove it (keep only the line-level ENV row)

Lines containing `"HMRC"` in the description: `item_no = "FEE"`, same qty derivation.

### Return-Only Content Lines

A return-only line is any content invoice line where cylinders are returned but none are delivered (`qty_shipped = 0`, `qty_returned > 0`). This includes both individual return lines within an otherwise normal invoice and invoices where every line is a return.

For return-only lines, set all fields as follows:

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| `qty` | `0` |
| `qty_shipped` | `0` |
| `qty_returned` | Actual count of cylinders returned |
| `unit_price` | `0` |
| `line_amount` | `0` |
| `item_no` | Product code as printed — populate normally |
| `description` | Product description as printed — populate normally |

**Whole-invoice returns:** When every line on the invoice is a return, retain `document_type = content_invoice`. The `invoice_total` will be `$0.00`.

### Holston Gases — Cylinder Return/Pickup Rule

When `Cyl_Shipped = 0` AND `Cyl_Returned > 0` AND `Line_Amount = 0 / blank / "N"`, this is a cylinder return/pickup transaction. Assign `item_no = "910013"` for these rows rather than dropping them.

---

## Extended Extraction Rules

### Item_No Transformations

Apply GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME §13.3 normalization pipeline. Content-specific steps for §13.3 Step 3:
- **Strip prefixes** (case-insensitive, longest-match first): `ESPRIGAS`, `ESPRI` — **not** `USP` (retained as of 2026-10-02; see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §13.3 Step 1)
- If the line is a rental item on a mixed invoice, **append `-R`**
- If a content line result ends in `-R` (not a rental line), **strip the hyphen** — retain the `R` (e.g., `GAS-R` → `GASR`)

**Vendors without a printed product code** — derive `item_no` from the description field: apply ChangeAbbreviation, remove spaces, then truncate to the vendor-specific limit:

| Vendor | Char Limit | Notes |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| PARACO / PARACO GAS | (full) | Apply ChangeAbbreviation to full description |
| MAVERICK | 15 | |
| APPLEOXYGEN | 15 | No ChangeAbbreviation — use raw characters |
| CLINICAL | 20 | |
| MESSER | 25 | Non-rental |
| WESTCO | 25 | |

> **Propane line identification note:** When checking whether a line is a propane line, check the description for `"PROPANE"` (case-insensitive). `item_no`-based detection (`"PRO"` prefix) is also valid since ChangeAbbreviation is now applied at extraction time.

### `esprigas_item_no` — Always Empty

**Write `esprigas_item_no: ""` on every content invoice and propane invoice line.** Rosetta's role here is to capture the supplier's printed part number accurately into `item_no` (normalized per §13.3 above) — not to compute or report what EspriGas's own item number should be. A separate lookup inside Atlas performs cross-reference matching downstream, and Business Central holds the ultimate, authoritative mapping logic.

The GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §13.4 resolution algorithm (fee mapping, bulk gas mapping, cross-reference lookup, §13.8 scheme construction) still runs internally where another rule needs its result — Fee/Resource Mapping to identify delivery/hazmat/fuel-surcharge lines, Bulk Gas Product Mapping for the propane-split decision, and the `910019` Rush Delivery code for `is_rush` detection. **None of that resolved value is ever written to the output line object** — the key is always present with value `""`; never write the resolved code or `"NOT IDENTIFIED"` in its place. This applies to the content sub-invoice and the propane sub-invoice of a Mixed Invoice as well. Rental Invoices (including a Mixed Invoice's rental sub-invoice) and Purchase Orders also always write `""` — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §13.4 Output value policy.

### AmeriGas — Supplier Account Extraction

When the seller name contains `"amerigas"`, the account number is not a standalone field. Scan all Description cells for the pattern `"SITE"` followed by contiguous digits:

```
"SITE12345" → account = "12345"
```

Extract only if splitting on `"SITE"` yields exactly two parts. Use the digit string immediately following `"SITE"` as `supplier_account_no`.

### ROCKYMOUNT — Non-Rental Sparse Table Removal

On non-rental ROCKYMOUNT invoices, discard any table that has 4 or fewer distinct column labels. These are page header artifacts.

### AIRGAS — Item Number Validation and Account Number

On non-rental Airgas invoices, if any `item_no` value consists entirely of digits, flag the document with `"(-10) Item_Number Error"` and deduct −10 from the confidence score. A valid Airgas `item_no` contains letters.

**`supplier_account_no`** (all Airgas invoice types): Use the number printed immediately after `"SHIP TO:"` in the bottom-left section of the invoice (e.g., `SHIP TO: 3867758` → `3867758`). Do **not** use the `SOLD TO NO.` or `PAYER` fields in the top header — those are TMG's master billing codes, not the location-specific account number.

### Item_Price and Qty Derivation

Unit price and quantity arithmetic derivations are handled in post-processing. See the Post-Processing Reference section at the end of this file.

### Multi-PO Priority

Some vendors print two PO fields in the invoice header — a **Gas PO** and a **Hardgoods PO** (or similar split). When two PO fields are present:

- If both are populated and differ: use the **Gas PO** as `customer_po_number`; record the Hardgoods PO in `notes`.
- If both are populated and identical: use either; no note required.
- If only one is populated: use it as `customer_po_number` regardless of type.

### Cylinder Sales — UOM=CYL

**Scope — vendor-invocation required, not a general rule.** `UOM = CYL` is the standard exchange unit for most vendors and must **not** be treated as a sale signal by default; the `qty_returned` field rules above intentionally do not use UOM as a general purchase indicator for this reason. Apply this rule **only** for a vendor whose section explicitly invokes it by name (currently: Tech-Gas Solutions — see Extended Extraction Rules). The check is made against the document's as-printed UOM at extraction time, before the `unit` output field is normalized to `EA`.

For a vendor where this rule is invoked, lines with printed UOM = `CYL` are outright cylinder sales, not cylinder exchanges:

- Set `qty_returned = 0`
- Exclude from footer cylinder totals (e.g., `TOTAL CYLINDERS SHIPPED / RETURNED`)

### Bulk Gas Product Lines

Lines where UOM indicates a bulk delivery (GAL, GALLON, LB, LBS) and the product is not a cylinder fill are bulk gas product lines. Cylinder sale lines (UOM=CYL) are not bulk gas — see §Cylinder Sales above.

Assign `esprigas_item_no` for these lines from GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME §18.4. Key UOM signals:
- `GAL`, `GALLON` → bulk liquid oxygen or bulk propane
- `LB`, `LBS` → bulk dry ice or bulk CO2 (by weight)

### Vendor-Specific Rules

#### CARBONIC SERVICE INC — Item_No Logic (Non-Rental)

Non-rental invoices:
- `item_no` = first 14 characters of Description, spaces removed (preserve existing OCR value if already present and non-blank).
- `qty` defaults to `"1"` if empty.
- `item_price` = copy of `line_amount` value (unit price equals line total when qty = 1).

#### DESERT ISLE — Item_No from Description Pattern

Item_No extracted using regex: `Charge\s*([^/]*?)\s*(?:/|Cylinders)` (case-insensitive).
Validate captured value starts with a digit. Apply ChangeAbbreviation.

Example: `"Charge MEDICAL OXYGEN / 220 CF"` → `"MEDOXY"`

---

## Vendor Reference

### Vern Lewis Welding Supply
- **EspriGas Account:** Extract from the **Ship To Account No.** field — **not** the Sold To Account No. — per the general Sold To / Ship To preference rule above.
  > **Corrected 2026-10-02:** Extraction had been pulling the Sold To Account No. instead, per Chris Farmer's review. The previously documented value `7201563` was recorded as "(Sold To address)" and has not been reverified against the correct Ship To field — treat it as unconfirmed until a sample invoice showing both fields side-by-side is checked.
- **Invoice format:** Multi-column layout with INVOICE, DATE, LOCATION, ITEM, QTY, DESCRIPTION, UNITS, PRICE, AMOUNT columns
- **Standard fees:** ESPRIDELIVERY $12.00, FUEL SURCHARGE $5.00, HYDRO TEST MAINTENANCE $14.50/ea, COMPLIANCE FEE $4.50/ea, ACETREQUAL $25.00/ea
- **Special items:** PRO-33 (Fork Lift Propane 33#/8 Gal @ $28.50) appears on HS 15602 and HS 15659
- **Customers:** Arizona HVAC/refrigeration — Goodman Distribution, RSD Peoria, RSD Phoenix, Trane Tech, United Refrigeration, Johnstone Supply locations

### Analgesic Services Inc. (Content Invoices)
- **EspriGas Accounts:** 2574 (VCA - Cypress Animal Hospital), 2580 (VCA Loomis Basin), 2378 (Folsom Endoscopy Center)
- **Invoice format:** "ORIGINAL INVOICE" header with standard column layout
- **Cylinder quantity columns:** `CYLINDER SHP'D` → `qty_shipped`; `CYL RET'D` → `qty_returned`
- **RELEASE # field:** Ignore — contains an internal EspriGas identifier (e.g., `"ESPRI"`), not extractable data
- **Lot numbers** appear on content invoice lines — these are cylinder serial/lot identifiers, not line items to extract

### Helget Gas Products (HELGET)
- **Item code format:** Printed as two space-separated tokens — a gas-type prefix and a number (e.g. `"O2 34742"`). **Capture both tokens as `item_no`** — do not drop the gas-type prefix and capture only the trailing number.
  > **Corrected 2026-10-02:** Extraction had been capturing only the number (e.g. `34742` instead of `O2 34742`), per Chris Farmer's review.
- **Space handling exception:** Per GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §13.3 Step 2, do **not** remove the space between the two tokens — `item_no = "O2 34742"`, not `"O234742"`. This is a documented, named exception to the otherwise-unconditional space-removal step.

### Holston Gases
- **EspriGas Account:** B6046
- **Filename quirk:** Filename contains `%0A` (URL-encoded newline). Use glob pattern `Cust*` to locate.
- **Credit memos:** Holston issues credit memos as invoices with negative totals (e.g., Invoice 308440, -$22.00 for a delivery charge at Lanesville Food Mart). These must be routed to `credit_memo_extraction.md` — do not extract as a Content Invoice.

### Southeastern Medical Equipment
- **EspriGas Account:** Derived — `"SME"` + Ship-To street number. Example: 8715 Owenfield Drive → `SME8715`
- **Invoice format:** Simple table (Item, Description, Qty, Rate, Amt). Medical equipment and supplies, NOT gas fills.
- **Freight:** Included as a line item (item code FREIGHT)
- **Tracking number → `tracking_number`:** Printed as `TRACKING #{number}` (e.g., `TRACKING #1Z5WW0320335636545` — UPS format), typically in the invoice footer. Strip the `TRACKING` label — output only `#1Z5WW0320335636545` into `tracking_number`. Omit `tracking_number` entirely when no tracking number is present.
- **Page 2:** UPS tracking numbers — not a separate document. Extract the tracking number into `tracking_number` (per the rule above — `#` + code only, no `TRACKING` label) on the invoice's own output record rather than discarding the page.

### Rocky Mountain Air Solutions
- **EspriGas Account:** Bill-To account number printed on invoice (e.g., 52458)
- **Invoice format:** Multi-page with Ordered/Shipped/Remaining/Returned qty columns, Contract Name and Line Number references
- **Standard fees:** LOCAL DELIVERY 3, FUEL SURCHARGE, HZ GAS (hazmat)
- **Maintenance:** UT-TEST (UltraSonic Cylinder Test-Pass, $20.55/ea)

### Coastal Carbonic (Content Invoices)
- **EspriGas Account:** Numeric (e.g., 530357)
- **Content invoice format:** Standard table (Product, CF/Lbs, Qty Ordered, B.O., Shipped, Returned, Unit Price, Amount). Bulk CO2 billed by weight in LBS.
- **CO2-DEMAND:** A $0.00 demand charge line — extract it as a valid line with $0 amount
- **Bill-To quirk:** May bill to an EspriGas regional address rather than College Station HQ — still EspriGas as Bill-To

### Jackson Welding Supply Co., Inc.
- **EspriGas Account:** Sold-To account number (e.g., 476650)
- **Invoice format:** Stock Number, Description, Quantity (CF total), Unit Price, Cylinders Shp/Rtn, Amount. Billing quantity is **cylinder count (Shp column)**, not CF total.
- **Delivery lines:** DEL / Truck Charge lines at $0.00 — include them
- **customer_po_number:** Follows Multi-PO Priority rule above — Gas PO takes precedence.

### Tech-Gas Solutions (TECHGAS)

Header band fields:
- `ORDER #` (e.g., `0000147497-00`) → `order_no`
- `CUS P/O #` (e.g., `40107071`) → `customer_po_number`
- `GAS P/O #` — if populated, note in `notes`

These fields appear on the same header band as TERMS, BRN, INITIALS, and PAGE. Extract from this band.

**Shipping Order Number Decoding:** The ITEM column encodes order number, date, and item code as a single concatenated string. Structure: leading digits = order number, next 4 digits = `MMDD` date, remaining characters = item code.

- `ship_date`: Read the 4-digit date portion as `MMDD` of the invoice year. Example: `1498340512NIT40` → date digits `0512` → `ship_date = 05/12/{invoice_year}`.
- `item_no`: Strip all leading digits from the ITEM string; if the result begins with `ZZ`, strip that prefix too. Apply standard normalization (remove `ESPRI` and `USP`, then remove spaces). Examples: `1498340512NIT40` → `NIT40`; `1498340512ZZ FUELSUR` → strip digits → `ZZ FUELSUR` → strip `ZZ` → `FUELSUR`; `1498340512ZZ DELIVERY FEE` → strip `ZZ` → `DELIVERYFEE`.

**Cylinder Quantities:** TECHGAS repurposes the QTY B/O column for cylinder returns rather than back-order quantities.

- `qty_shipped` → QTY SHIP'D column (product lines only; output `0` for fee lines)
- `qty_returned` → QTY B/O column (product lines only; output `0` for fee lines)

**Cylinder Sales:** Lines with `UOM = CYL` — apply the Cylinder Sales rule (see Extended Extraction Rules above). Additionally, these lines have no `QTY B/O` row (the column is repurposed for returns on exchange lines only).

**Tariff Fees:** Fee lines where the description contains `"TARIFF"` are cylinder-type-specific charges billed on purchased (sold) cylinders. The invoice prints `qty=1` on the tariff line as a lump sum — ignore this printed qty. For these lines:
- `qty` = total quantity from **cylinder sale lines only** (UOM=CYL) for the matching cylinder size on the same invoice. Do **not** include exchange lines (UOM=EA).
- `unit_price` = `line_amount ÷ qty`

**Example (Invoice 0000357255):**
- `60 TARIFF` line_amount=62.50; NIT60CYL qty=5 → tariff qty=5, unit_price=$12.50
- `20 TARIFF` line_amount=40.50; OXY20CYL qty=6 → tariff qty=6, unit_price=$6.75

| Fee Item | Applies To | `esprigas_item_no` |
|----------|-----------|-------------------|
| MCTARIFF | MC Acetylene — CYL sale lines (ACTMCCYL) | 930088 |
| 20TARIFF | 20 CF — CYL sale lines (e.g., OXY20CYL, NIT20CYL) | 930081 |
| 40TARIFF | 40 CF — CYL sale lines (e.g., NIT40CYL, OXY40CYL) | 930082 |
| 60TARIFF | 60 CF — CYL sale lines (e.g., NIT60CYL, OXY60CYL) | 930083 |
| 80TARIFF | 80 CF — CYL sale lines (e.g., NIT80CYL, OXY80CYL) | 930084 |
| 125TARIFF | 125 CF — CYL sale lines (e.g., NIT125CYL, OXY125CYL) | 930085 |
| 150TARIFF | 150 CF — CYL sale lines (e.g., NIT150CYL, OXY150CYL) | 930086 |
| 300TARIFF | 300 CF — CYL sale lines (e.g., NIT300CYL, OXY300CYL) | 930087 |

### United Welding Supply Co.

Two PO fields in header: `Hardgoods PO #` and `Gas PO #`. Apply the Multi-PO Priority rule — see Extended Extraction Rules above.

### Irish Carbonic Company (IRISHCARBONIC)

**Item number prefix:** Irish Carbonic item numbers carry a `ZZZ` prefix (e.g., `ZZZENERGY`, `ZZZSCBULK`). Strip the `ZZZ` prefix before writing `item_no` to the output — do not apply the standard `ESPRIGAS` / `ESPRI` / `USP` normalization to these items.

**Known item mappings:**

| Raw Item No. | Normalized `item_no` | Notes |
|-------------|---------------------|-------|
| `ZZZENERGY` | `ENERGY` | Energy surcharge line |
| `ZZZSCBULK` | `SCBULK` | Bulk CO2 service charge line |

Apply the same stripping rule to any other `ZZZ`-prefixed items encountered — strip `ZZZ` and use the remainder as `item_no`.

### NuCara Home Medical (NUCARA)

**Invoice format:** "Group Bill" — a single PDF bundling multiple discrete rental and content invoices across multiple customer locations. Each page may contain one or more invoice sections under a patient/location group header.

**Classification within Group Bill:** A page section is a NuCara content invoice when it contains `O2 E CONTENTS` or `DELIVERY CHARGE` item codes. Sections containing only `O2TANKRENTAL` → route to rent_invoice extractor.

**Summary page discard:** Pages showing ONLY "Branch Total" or "Patient Total" row(s) with no individual invoice sections (i.e., no `"Invoice: XXXXXX"` entries) → discard; do not extract.

**supplier_account_no:** Extract from the patient/location group header row — the ID# printed in the upper right of the Description column header. Example: `"ESPRIGAS - DAVITA AMES MARY   ID: 138441"` → `supplier_account_no = "138441"`.

**customer_name:** Group header label, excluding the `"ESPRIGAS - "` prefix. Example: `"ESPRIGAS - DAVITA ANKENY DIALYSIS"` → `"DaVita Ankeny Dialysis"`.

**customer_po_number:** From the `"PO:"` field on each individual invoice section header (e.g., `"Invoice: 3280473  PO: 12345"`).

**invoice_date:** Use the Group Bill document date printed on each page (e.g., `"Date: 9/3/2025"`). Do not substitute service period dates as invoice_date.

**delivery_date:** Extract from the `"Date Range"` column printed on each content invoice section. The start and end dates are always identical — use either date as `delivery_date`.

**invoice_total / Charges Amt vs. Balance:** NuCara Group Bills include two amount columns — `"Charges Amt"` (original charge) and `"Balance"` (outstanding after any applied credits or payments). Use the **Balance** column to compute `invoice_total` (sum of Balance amounts for all lines in the invoice). Do **NOT** use Charges Amt as invoice_total. When Balance < Charges Amt for any line in an invoice, add flag: `"pre_payment_applied — original charges: $X; balance: $Y; invoice_total reflects outstanding balance"`. For `line_amount`: use the Charges Amt column per line (to preserve accurate unit_price and qty arithmetic). When the `pre_payment_applied` flag is present, the line amount sum will not equal invoice_total — this is expected; do not additionally raise a §17 reconciliation flag for this discrepancy.

**alt po#:** NuCara prints an `"alt po#"` reference in some invoice section headers — purpose not yet defined. Capture in `order_no` if present; leave `order_no` blank if absent.

### Indiana Oxygen Co. (INDIANAOXY)

- **EspriGas Accounts:** Multiple — see supplier_account_crossref. (e.g., W7072)
- **Trade Partner:** INSTANTLRN (not in §TP.2) — **superseded by §3.10**: newer files carry a `TradePartner` column directly (Priority 1); older files without that column fall back to the `IndyOxy_` filename prefix (Priority 2) if present. See §3.10 for current behavior.
- **Partner Name:** No dedicated vendor-name column exists in this CSV format — populated via §3.11 from whichever source §3.10 resolved for `trade_partner` (the `TradePartner` column when present, otherwise the filename prefix).
- **Invoice format:** CSV export. One row per line item. Multiple invoices grouped by invoice number within a single file. Apply §3 CSV / Flat File Processing rules.

#### CSV Format

| CSV Column Header | Schema Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `TradePartner` | `trade_partner` / `partner_name` | **Newer file formats only** — when present, this is Priority 1 per §3.10/§3.11: use directly for both fields (verbatim, no normalization), ahead of the filename-prefix fallback. Older Indiana Oxygen files predate this column — see §3.10 Priority 2 for those. |
| `Invoice` | `invoice_no` | Group key — all rows sharing this value form one invoice; apply §13.6 normalization |
| `Invoice Date` | `invoice_date` | |
| `Match` | *(ignore)* | Internal field |
| `PO Number` | `customer_po_number` | Apply §13.10 normalization |
| `Order Number` | `order_no` | |
| `Delivery Ticket Number` | *(ignore)* | No schema field |
| `Account Number` | `supplier_account_no` | EspriGas account with Indiana Oxygen |
| `Ship To Name 1` | `customer_name` | |
| `Ship To City` | `customer_address.city` | |
| `Ship To State` | `customer_address.state` | |
| `Ship To Zip` | `customer_address.zip` | |
| `Line Items Description` | `description` | |
| `Line Items Item Price` | `unit_price` | |
| `Line Items Line Amount` | `line_amount` | |
| `Totals Total` | `invoice_total` | Summary row — read value, then discard row per §3.3 |
| `Line Items Qty` | `qty_shipped` | |
| `Line Items Cyl Returned` | `qty_returned` | Dedicated return column — extract directly; §3.6 negative-qty pattern does not apply |
| `Line Items Item No` | `item_no` | Apply §13.3 normalization pipeline |
| `Content Type` | *(routing classifier)* | Determines invoice type. `"Content"` → apply this extractor. Rental value TBD — route to rent_invoice extractor when confirmed. |
| `Fulfillment Date` | `ship_date` / `delivery_date` | Use as both; add `"ship_date_derived_from_table"` flag per §15.5a |

**Address note:** Indiana Oxygen CSV does not include a street address column. Omit `address_1` and `address_2` subfields — do not write empty strings.

**CSV routing:** When processing an IndyOxy CSV batch, inspect the `Content Type` column before extraction. Group rows by invoice number, then route each invoice group to the appropriate extractor based on its `Content Type` value. Content invoices apply these rules; rental invoices apply `rent_invoice_extraction.md` rules. The rental `Content Type` label is not yet confirmed — update both this section and the INDIANAOXY section in `rent_invoice_extraction.md` once a rental sample is reviewed.

**`Our Truck` lines:** A delivery fee line despite its minimal printed description (`"1 "`). After §13.3 normalization (space removal), `item_no = "OurTruck"`. Per `content_invoice_extraction.md`'s `esprigas_item_no` — Always Empty policy, do not resolve or write a code here — leave `esprigas_item_no: ""` like every other line. `"OurTruck"` is a valid entry for the downstream cross-reference table (→ 910005 Delivery); that mapping lives there now, not in this extraction rule.

**Cylinder sale lines:** `CYL10`, `CYL20`, `CYL40` in `Line Items Item No` indicate outright cylinder sales — set `qty_returned = 0` per hardgoods purchase rule regardless of the `Line Items Cyl Returned` column value.

#### PDF Format — "ORIGINAL INVOICE" Layout

Indiana Oxygen also issues a distinct PDF invoice format (letterhead reads `"ORIGINAL INVOICE"` / `"INDIANA OXYGEN CO."`), separate from the CSV export above. Column mapping for this layout:

| Printed Column | Schema Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ITEM` | `item_no` | Apply §13.3 normalization pipeline |
| `QTY INV'D` | *(not extracted)* | Internal invoiced-unit count — does not map to `qty`, `qty_shipped`, or `qty_returned`. Do not use it to satisfy any "always include" or non-zero-quantity condition in Zero-Dollar Line Filtering. |
| `QTY BO` | *(not extracted)* | Backorder count — same treatment as `QTY INV'D` above |
| `CYLINDER — SHP'D` | `qty_shipped` | |
| `CYLINDER — RET'D` | `qty_returned` | |
| `DESCRIPTION` | `description` | |
| `UOM` | `uom` | |
| `UNIT PRICE` | `unit_price` | |
| `AMOUNT` | `line_amount` | |

**"Cylinder Return" annotation row — do not extract as a line item.** This format prints a standalone row reading `"Cylinder Return"` in both `ITEM` and `DESCRIPTION`, with `QTY INV'D = 1` and every other numeric column blank or `$0.00`. This is the Non-Billable Annotation Row pattern (Zero-Dollar Line Filtering, above, applies to any supplier) — a restatement of the return activity already captured on the product line(s) above (e.g. `CD20FG`'s own `RET'D` count), the same class as the `"Cylinder Shipped Total:"` / `"Cylinder Returned Total:"` footer rows beneath it. Discard all three; per the column mapping above, `QTY INV'D` is never extracted, so it can never satisfy a non-zero-quantity exception.

**Shipping/Handling totals-block fee.** This format commonly prints `$0.00` on every extracted product line, with the entire invoice amount carried in a `Shipping/Handling` field in the totals block — apply GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §18.6 (Totals-Block Fee Promotion) to capture it as a line.

### Xpedited Gas Inc. (XPEDITEDGAS)

- **Supplier Name 2:** Naples FL
- **Vendor Nos:** V003578 (Parent), V003581
- **Trade Partner:** XPEDITEDGAS (post-processing reference via Section A; not yet in §TP.2 model-layer lookup — output will resolve to INSTANTLRN until added)

- **`supplier_account_no`:** Xpedited's account number for the delivery location — read directly from the invoice header

### General Air Service & Supply (GENERALAIR)

General Air Content Invoices do not print an order/shipping-order number field of any kind. Its absence is expected for this vendor, not an extraction gap — do not apply the "Missing optional field" confidence deduction to `order_no` on General Air content invoices (see Confidence Scoring — Minor Flags above). `ship_via` absence is unaffected and still deducts normally when absent.

For General Air content invoices, exclude any line where **both** `unit_price = 0.00` and `line_amount = 0.00`, regardless of `qty_shipped`, `qty_returned`, or line type. This overrides the general Zero-Dollar Line Filtering rule (including its `qty_returned > 0` always-include exception) for this vendor only — see Zero-Dollar Line Filtering above.

For General Air content invoices, do not apply the "No product lines" −10 confidence deduction (Confidence Scoring — Integrity Checks), even when zero-dollar-line exclusion above leaves only fee/charge lines — **provided §17 line total reconciliation still passes** (`sum(line_amounts) = invoice_total`). If reconciliation fails, apply both the line total reconciliation deduction and the No product lines deduction as normal.

## Account Number Derivation Rules

| Vendor | Rule | Example |
|--------|------|---------|
| Southeastern Medical Equipment | `"SME"` + Ship-To street number | 8715 Owenfield Dr → `SME8715` |
| AmeriGas | Digits immediately following `"SITE"` in any line item description | `"SITE12345"` → `12345` |
| AIRGAS (AIRGASNATIONAL) | Number immediately following `"SHIP TO:"` in the bottom-left section of the invoice | `SHIP TO: 3867758` → `3867758` |
| SJ Smith (SJSMITH) | Concatenate: `temp_route` + `"-"` + `temp_route1` | `"015141"` + `"-"` + `"44"` → `015141-44` |
| Delta Gases (DELTAGASES) | Concatenate: `temp_route` prefix + `supplier_account_no` field value | Route prefix + account suffix |

## Customer-Specific Extraction Rules

### PF Changs

**Applies to:** Any invoice where the Ship-To customer is a PF Changs location (customer name contains `"PF CHANG"`).

**Fuel Surcharge — Force qty=1:** Regardless of how the supplier calculates the fuel surcharge (e.g., volume × per-unit rate), extract fuel surcharge lines with:
- `qty = 1`
- `unit_price = line_amount`

> **Example (Airgas Dry Ice Invoice 9173726085):** Supplier prints `SURCHARGE FUEL 105*0.01910=2.01`; extract as `qty=1`, `unit_price=2.01`, `line_amount=2.01`.

> **Override note:** This takes precedence over the AIRGAS DRY ICE general rule (§Post-Processing — "all other lines: qty=first_row_qty") for fuel surcharge lines on PF Changs accounts.

## Multi-Delivery Content Invoice Splitting

Some vendors issue a single invoice covering multiple distinct delivery events within the same billing period, and may additionally include monthly or daily recurring rental charges alongside those deliveries. When this pattern is detected, the invoice must be split into individual output records — one per delivery event, plus one for all recurring rental charges if present. This rule applies to all suppliers.

### Identifying Delivery Lines vs. Recurring Lines

Classify each line by its billing structure:

| Line Type | Criteria | Typical UOM | Examples |
|-----------|----------|-------------|---------|
| **Delivery line** | Single date in Start column; no End date | EA, HR | Oxygen fills (S8120), Hazmat charge (3009), Scheduled delivery (A9900), RT evaluations (D247), per-unit cylinder sales |
| **Recurring line** | Date range (Start + End dates) | MO, DA | Monthly cylinder rent (D207, D208), daily concentrator (4300), daily BIPAP/ventilator (4572), daily nebulizer (4714) |

Fee lines (Hazmat, delivery charge, scheduled delivery) bearing the **same single date** as a delivery event travel with that delivery's output record.

### Split Trigger

Split when **either** condition is true:
1. Any two content lines have different DATE column values — do not consolidate lines with different dates into a single output record. Each distinct date becomes its own `-Cn` record.
2. The invoice contains **both** delivery lines (any date) **and** recurring rental lines.

### Grouping and Output Records

1. All recurring lines → one **Rental** output record (`document_type: "rent_invoice"`, `content_type: "Rent"`). The `-R` output follows `rent_invoice_extraction.md` rules for all field values. If the recurring lines contain multiple distinct rental period date ranges (e.g., Apr 1–Apr 30 and May 1–May 31 on the same source invoice), add flag `"(-5) multiple_rental_periods_detected — manual review required"` to `confidence.flags`. **PLACEHOLDER — REVIEW PENDING:** Invoices with multiple distinct rental periods may need to be split into one `-R` output per period; rules to be defined when sample documents are reviewed.
2. All delivery lines sharing the same date, plus any same-date fee lines → one **Content** output record (`document_type: "content_invoice"`, `content_type: "Content"`) per unique delivery date.
3. **Undated fee lines** (fee lines with no associated delivery date, such as Hazmat or Fuel Charge printed at the bottom of the invoice with no date column): when `fee_qty = number_of_content_outputs`, distribute one fee line per content record at qty=1 and the original unit_price. When `fee_qty ≠ number_of_content_outputs`, attach all undated fee lines to the `-C1` record and flag `"(-5) undated_fee_qty_mismatch — manual review required"` with a −5 deduction.

### Invoice Number Suffixes

| Output | `invoice_no` |
|--------|-------------|
| Rental (recurring lines) | `{source_invoice_no}-R` |
| Delivery — 1st date (chronological) | `{source_invoice_no}-C1` |
| Delivery — 2nd date | `{source_invoice_no}-C2` |
| Delivery — Nth date | `{source_invoice_no}-CN` |

> If no recurring lines exist — only multiple delivery dates — omit the `-R` record. Number deliveries `-C1`, `-C2`, etc. in chronological order.
>
> If only one delivery date exists alongside recurring lines, the single content record uses suffix `-C1`.

### Past Due Allocation

Past due balance attaches to the `-R` (rental) record. If no rental record is produced, attach to `-C1`.

### `source_file_output_total`

Count all output records produced from this source invoice: rental record (if any) + number of distinct delivery dates. All output records from the same source invoice carry the same `source_file_output_total` value.

**Example:** An invoice with rental lines and two delivery dates → `source_file_output_total = 3` on all three output records.

### Worked Example

Invoice BBTV2J1F (Avalon CC Pasco, Pasco WA) contains:

- Recurring lines (5/01–5/31/26): D208 cylinders, helium cylinders, BIPAP, humidifier
- Delivery lines dated 4/28/26: D202 oxygen fills + hazmat + scheduled delivery charge
- Delivery lines dated 5/14/26: D202 oxygen fills + hazmat + scheduled delivery charge

Produces 3 output records (`source_file_output_total: 3`):

| Output | Lines included | Current | Past Due | Total |
|--------|---------------|--------:|---------:|------:|
| BBTV2J1F-R | D208 + helium + BIPAP + humidifier | $642.97 | $665.69 | $1,308.66 |
| BBTV2J1F-C1 | 4/28/26 — D202 + hazmat + delivery | $121.71 | $0.00 | $121.71 |
| BBTV2J1F-C2 | 5/14/26 — D202 + hazmat + delivery | $116.84 | $0.00 | $116.84 |

Reconciliation: $642.97 + $121.71 + $116.84 = $881.52 ✓ (original invoice subtotal)

---

## Bulk Propane Gallon Customers

The following ship-to customers purchase propane exclusively, billed by the gallon using EspriGas item# `71100C`. All gas lines for these customers receive `esprigas_item_no = "71100C"`. Non-gas lines (delivery, fuel surcharge, hazmat, and other fees) are extracted normally.

**All other bulk propane customers** (not in this list) use `esprigas_item_no = "71100B"`. See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME §18.4 for the full bulk gas product code table.

**Customer list (match `customer_name` case-insensitively):**
- Atlantic Plywood
- Fortna
- Parksite

**document_type and content_type:** These customers produce a standard content invoice output — `document_type: "content_invoice"`, and therefore `content_type: "Content"` per GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §20. `document_type: "propane_invoice"` (and its derived `content_type: "Propane"`) is reserved exclusively for customers who trigger the Propane Invoice Split (§14.1). The Propane Invoice Split section does **not** apply to these customers — no split is generated. Do not add these customers to the §14.1 Propane Split Customer list.

**33# propane tank conversion:**

**Applies only when `partner_name` normalizes to `ATLANTAPROPANE` or `FERRELLGAS`.** For all other suppliers, extract the line as-is without conversion even if the customer is in the bulk propane gallon customer list.

When an invoice line for a bulk propane gallon customer (above) from one of these suppliers shows propane in a 33-pound tank format — identified by the description or item_no containing `"33#"`, `"33 LB"`, or `"33LB"` (case-insensitive) — apply the following conversion before writing the output line. The `"PROPANE"` keyword check is not required: all gas lines for these customers are propane by definition.

| Field | Rule |
|-------|------|
| `qty` | `original_qty × 4` |
| `unit_price` | `original_unit_price ÷ 4` (preserves `line_amount`) |
| `line_amount` | **Unchanged** — must equal the original invoice line amount |
| `unit` | `GAL` |
| `esprigas_item_no` | `71100C` |

Add flag `"(0) 33lb_propane_converted_to_gal — qty×4"` to `confidence.flags` for each converted line. No confidence deduction — this is an expected conversion for these customers.

---

## Propane Invoice Split

> **Hard stop — check customer first.** Before performing any propane line detection, confirm the ship-to customer matches an entry in the Propane Split Customer list (GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §14.1). If the customer is **not** listed, skip this section entirely and extract the invoice as a standard content invoice with no split. Many suppliers sell or exchange propane cylinders as a normal product line — the presence of propane items on an invoice does **not** trigger a split unless the specific ship-to customer is listed.

When the ship-to customer **is** confirmed in the Propane Split Customer list (GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §14.1), this extractor produces **two output records** from the single source invoice: a Content Invoice and a Propane Invoice.

### Step 1 — Identify propane lines

Apply GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME §14.2.

### Step 2 — Identify propane-specific surcharges

Apply GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME §14.3.

### Step 3 — Assign lines to outputs

| Line type | Output |
|-----------|--------|
| Propane cylinder exchange lines (§14.2) | Propane Invoice |
| Propane-specific surcharges (§14.3) | Propane Invoice |
| All other product lines | Content Invoice |
| Standard shared fees (Delivery, Fuel Surcharge, Hazmat, etc.) | Content Invoice |

### Step 4 — Derive invoice numbers

Invoice number suffixes (`-C`, `-R`, `-P`, `-C1`, `-C2`) are applied at extraction time per the split rules in this file and GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME §14.

### Step 5 — Reconcile totals

Apply GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME §14.5 to reconcile totals.

### APR / Rockstar Transco account override

If the ship-to customer is APR, apply GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME §14.6.

---

## Output Schema

**Output format:** Always return a JSON array — one element per extracted document. A propane split produces two elements: the Content Invoice record followed by the Propane Invoice record. See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §16.

```json
[
{
  "document_type": "content_invoice",
  "source_file_output_total": "integer — total output records expected from this source file (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §7.9)",
  "source_page_start": "integer — 1-indexed page number where this document begins in the source PDF/image; omit for CSV/flat-file input (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §7.10)",
  "source_rows": ["integer — 1-indexed file line numbers (header = line 1) contributing to this document; omit for PDF/image input (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §3.9)"],
  "required_fields_missing": ["string — Tier 1 field names absent from source document; omit this field entirely when all Tier 1 fields are present (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §15)"],
  "rosetta_version": "string (vX.XX — Rosetta Combined version used for this extraction)",
  "confidence": {
    "score": "integer (0–100)",
    "label": "HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW",
    "flags": ["string"]
  },
  "header": {
    "partner_name": "string",
    "supplier_account_no": "string",
    "espri_account_no": "string (omit when no override applies — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §14.4)",
    "supplier_name": "string (vendor's remit-to entity name — omit entirely with supplier_address when neither a remit-to block nor a general vendor address is present; see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §19)",
    "supplier_address": {
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string | null",
      "city": "string",
      "state": "string (2-letter code)",
      "zip": "string"
    },
    "ship_from_name": "string (vendor's shipping-origin branch/warehouse from a SHIP FROM block; omit entirely with ship_from_address when absent — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §26)",
    "ship_from_address": {
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string | null",
      "city": "string",
      "state": "string (2-letter code)",
      "zip": "string"
    },
    "invoice_no": "string",
    "invoice_date": "string (MM/DD/YYYY)",
    "invoice_total": "number",
    "terms": "string (normalized payment terms — e.g., NET 45, COD, DUE ON RECEIPT)",
    "due_date": "string (MM/DD/YYYY)",
    "bill_to_name": "string (billed customer's/EspriGas's name from a BILL TO block; omit entirely with bill_to_address when absent — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §26)",
    "bill_to_address": {
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string | null",
      "city": "string",
      "state": "string (2-letter code)",
      "zip": "string"
    },
    "customer_name": "string",
    "customer_address": {
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string | null",
      "city": "string",
      "state": "string (2-letter code)",
      "zip": "string"
    },
    "buyer_code": "string (vendor-printed buyer/branch code; empty string when absent — never restate supplier_account_no; see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §25)",
    "shipto_code": "string (vendor-printed ship-to location code; empty string when absent — never restate supplier_account_no; see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §25)",
    "delivery_note_no": "string (vendor's delivery note/delivery number; omit entirely when absent — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §24)",
    "bill_of_lading_no": "string (vendor's bill of lading number; kept separate from delivery_note_no even when identical; omit entirely when absent — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §24)",
    "trade_partner": "string",
    "customer_po_number": "string",
    "po_date": "string (MM/DD/YYYY) — extract from document; default: ship_date → delivery date → invoice_date",
    "order_no": "string",
    "ship_date": "string (MM/DD/YYYY)",
    "delivery_date": "string (MM/DD/YYYY)",
    "ship_via": "string",
    "tracking_number": "string (omit entirely when not present on the document — e.g., carrier tracking number; see vendor-specific notes)",
    "comment": "string (text following a literal \"Comment:\" label anywhere on the document; omit entirely when not present — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §28)",
    "is_rush": "boolean — true when an expedite signal is present in any header field; otherwise false (extracted, not derived — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §23.2)",
    "delivered_by": "string — carrier/delivering party, UPPERCASED; omit entirely when no carrier is named (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §23.3)",
    "care_of": "string — intermediary/forwarding party; C/O marker and any EspriGas/TMG identifier stripped; omit entirely when absent or when nothing remains after stripping (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §21)",
    "content_type": "Content (derived from document_type — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §20)",
    "additional_header_fields": [{"label": "string — as printed on document", "value": "string — as printed on document"}, "omit entirely when none found — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §27"]
  },
  "lines": [
    {
      "item_no": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "qty": "number",
      "unit": "string (normalized to \"EA\" except bulk gas lines, which keep their printed unit — see Content Invoice Line Fields)",
      "unit_price": "number",
      "line_amount": "number",
      "qty_ordered": "number (omit field entirely when vendor does not provide ordered quantity)",
      "qty_shipped": "number",
      "qty_shipped_provenance": "stated | defaulted | not_applicable",
      "qty_returned": "integer",
      "qty_returned_provenance": "stated | defaulted | not_applicable",
      "esprigas_item_no": "string — always empty string (\"\"); placeholder for EspriGas item# populated in a later step — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §13.4",
      "xref_source": "null (reserved for future cross-reference source tracking; always output null)"
    }
  ]
}
]
```
