# SOURCE: credit_memo_extraction_v1.23.md
---

# Credit Memo — Extraction Logic
**Version:** 1.24
**Model Target:** claude-sonnet-5-5
**Min Token Estimate:** ~2,560
**Cache Strategy:** explicit
**Last Updated:** 2026-09-23

---

## Purpose

Classifies and extracts Credit Memo documents — vendor-issued records that reduce amounts owed, typically to reverse or partially reverse a prior invoice. Credit memos carry negative net values and may reference the original invoice being credited.

**Classification takes priority over other invoice types.** A document that would otherwise classify as a Content Invoice, Rental Invoice, or Mixed Invoice must be reclassified as a Credit Memo if it carries an explicit credit memo label or a negative invoice total.

**Repository routing:** After full extraction, credit memo output is routed to the Credit Memo Repository for downstream reconciliation (a post-processing step, not part of model-time extraction). Credit memos are not short-circuited — extraction always runs before routing.

---

## Classification Signals

A page is a Credit Memo when it matches **at least one** of the following:

### Primary Signals (either alone is sufficient)
| Signal | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| Document header contains `"CREDIT MEMO"`, `"CREDIT NOTE"`, `"CREDIT INVOICE"`, or `"CREDIT MEMORANDUM"` | Explicit label in the header block |
| The phrase `"CREDIT MEMO"` or `"CREDIT NOTE"` appears directly above or immediately preceding the line items section | Inline credit label, not in the main header |
| Invoice total (the `AMOUNT THIS INVOICE` or equivalent total field) is a **negative value** | Shown as a negative number or in parentheses |
| Invoice total is followed by `CR` (e.g., `151.91 CR`) | `CR` suffix indicates a credit balance; line items may individually appear as positive amounts |

### Supporting Signals (use to confirm when primary signals are ambiguous)
| Signal | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| Document references a prior invoice number with language like `"RE: INVOICE"`, `"CREDIT FOR INVOICE"`, `"APPLIES TO INVOICE"` | Cross-reference to the original invoice being credited |
| `"REASON FOR CREDIT"` field present | Explicit credit justification field |

### Important Distinctions — Do NOT Classify as Credit Memo
| Scenario | Required Action |
|----------|----------------|
| One or more line items are negative but the overall invoice total is **positive** | **Do not classify as Credit Memo.** Classify by primary document type and flag for **manual review** — see Mixed-Sign Invoice Rule below |
| Invoice contains **both positive and negative** line item amounts (mixed signs) | Classify by primary document type and flag for **manual review** — see Mixed-Sign Invoice Rule below |
| A document has the word "credit" only in a payment terms field (e.g., `"NET CREDIT 30"`) | Not a Credit Memo — classify by primary document type |

### Mixed-Sign Invoice Rule

**Individual negative line items do not classify a document as a Credit Memo.** Negative line amounts represent returns, adjustments, or corrections within an otherwise normal invoice.

When any invoice (of any type) contains **both positive and negative line item amounts**:
1. Classify by primary document type using the normal header signals.
2. Append `"(-20) mixed_sign_lines — manual review required"` to `confidence.flags`.
3. Deduct **−20** from the confidence score.
4. Do **not** reclassify as Credit Memo on the basis of line-level signs alone.

The Credit Memo classification requires a document-level signal: an explicit credit memo label or a negative **invoice total**.

---

## Extraction Rules

### Header Fields

| Output Field | Source Field | Notes |
|-------------|-------------|-------|
| `vendor_name` | Vendor letterhead | General vendor identification, as used elsewhere on the document. See `supplier_name`/`supplier_address` below for the dedicated remit-to fields. |
| `partner_name` | Vendor letterhead | Supplier name as printed on the document, extracted verbatim per GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §2. Holds the **same supplier name** as `vendor_name` — populate **both** fields; neither substitutes for the other. `partner_name` is the canonical field for Trade Partner matching and for consistency with the invoice document types. Distinct from `supplier_name` below, which is the remit-to payee and may differ. |
| `supplier_name` / `supplier_address` | Remit-to block, or vendor letterhead address as fallback | See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §19. Omit both entirely when neither a remit-to block nor a general vendor address appears on the document. |
| `ship_from_name` / `ship_from_address` | `SHIP FROM` block, typically paired with a top-row `BILL TO` | See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §26. Omit both entirely when no `SHIP FROM` block appears on the document. |
| `invoice_no` | Invoice / Credit Memo number field | Use the credit memo number as-is |
| `invoice_date` | Invoice date field | MM/DD/YYYY |
| `supplier_account_no` | Account / Customer number field | Apply the Account Selection — Multiple Candidates logic below if the document yields more than one candidate |
| `bill_to_name` | Bill To block | If this block identifies the account using an EspriGas identifier (per GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §1), apply the Ship-To Name Identification / Ship-To Exclusion Rule from §1 to `ship_to_name` instead — `bill_to_name` itself is not subject to that rule |
| `bill_to_address` | Bill To block | Split into `address_1`, `address_2`, `city`, `state`, `zip` |
| `ship_to_name` | Ship To block | If this block identifies the account using an EspriGas identifier, apply the Ship-To Name Identification / Ship-To Exclusion Rule (GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §1) — see the EspriGas Direct Delivery Integrity Check below |
| `ship_to_address` | Ship To block | Split into `address_1`, `address_2`, `city`, `state`, `zip` |
| `original_invoice_no` | Reference field, if present | The invoice being credited; null if not stated |
| `order_no` | Order # field | |
| `terms` | Terms field | |
| `ship_via` | Ship Via field | |
| `comment` | Text following a literal `Comment:` label, anywhere on the document | See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §28. Omit entirely when no `Comment:` label is present. |
| `additional_header_fields` | Any other labeled header field on the document | See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §27. Omit entirely when none found — no confidence deduction. |

### Account Selection — Multiple Candidates

When a verified account number cannot be read directly from the document and a lookup by supplier + ship-to returns more than one candidate, use the `Account Status` field on each candidate to select the correct account:

| Scenario | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Exactly one candidate has `Account Status = Primary` | Select that account number automatically |
| No Primary candidates; exactly one candidate has `Account Status = Backup` | Select that Backup account number automatically |
| No Primary candidates; two or more candidates have `Account Status = Backup` | Flag document for **manual review** — do not select automatically |

> **Data availability note:** The account candidate database that supplies `Account Status` values is not yet available. This rule will take effect once access is provided. Until then, treat all unresolved multi-candidate account numbers as requiring manual review.

### Line Item Fields

Extract all line items individually.

| Output Field | Source Field | Notes |
|-------------|-------------|-------|
| `item_no` | ITEM column | Apply Item Number Normalization (see below) |
| `description` | DESCRIPTION column | |
| `uom` | UOM column | |
| `qty` | QTY SHIP'D column (or equivalent) | Store as-is; may be negative |
| `unit_price` | UNIT PRICE column | Store as a positive number — sign is conveyed by `line_amount` |
| `line_amount` | AMOUNT column | **Always store as a negative number.** If the document shows a positive amount on a credit memo, negate it in the output |
| `esprigas_item_no` | — | Always written as an empty string (`""`) — placeholder for EspriGas item#, populated in a later step, not resolved by Rosetta. See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §13.4 |

### Item Number Normalization

A narrower version of GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME §13.3 — Credit Memos do not get the full ChangeAbbreviation word-substitution table, only the prefix strip below:
1. Remove the prefix `ESPRIGAS`, `ESPRI`, or `USP` (longest match first, case-insensitive).
2. **Remove all remaining spaces from the result — unconditional.** Apply this even when step 1 found no prefix to remove; never skip it.

### Amount Sign Convention

Credit memos represent amounts owed back to EspriGas. All monetary output values must be stored as **negative numbers** regardless of how the source document displays them:
- If the source shows `(151.91)` → output `-151.91`
- If the source shows `151.91 CR` → output `-151.91`
- If the source shows `-151.91` → output `-151.91`
- If the source shows `151.91` (positive) on a document classified as Credit Memo → output `-151.91`

Apply this convention to `line_amount` and `invoice_total`.

### Invoice Total

Capture from the `AMOUNT THIS INVOICE INCLUDING TAX` field or equivalent total line. Store as a negative number per the sign convention above.

---

## Output Schema

**Output format:** Always return a JSON array — one element per extracted document. See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §16.

```json
[
{
  "document_type": "credit_memo",
  "source_file_output_total": "integer — total output records expected from this source file (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §7.9)",
  "source_page_start": "integer — 1-indexed page number where this document begins in the source PDF/image; omit for CSV/flat-file input (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §7.10)",
  "source_rows": ["integer — 1-indexed file line numbers (header = line 1) contributing to this document; omit for PDF/image input (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §3.9)"],
  "required_fields_missing": ["string — Tier 1 field names absent from source document; omit this field entirely when all Tier 1 fields are present (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §15)"],
  "rosetta_version": "string (vX.XX — Rosetta Combined version used for this extraction)",
  "confidence": {
    "score": "integer (0–100)",
    "label": "HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW",
    "flags": ["string"]
  },
  "header": {
    "vendor_name": "string",
    "partner_name": "string (supplier name as printed — same value as vendor_name; populate both, see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §2)",
    "supplier_name": "string (vendor's remit-to entity name — omit entirely with supplier_address when neither a remit-to block nor a general vendor address is present; see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §19)",
    "supplier_address": {
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string | null",
      "city": "string",
      "state": "string (2-letter code)",
      "zip": "string"
    },
    "ship_from_name": "string (vendor's shipping-origin branch/warehouse from a SHIP FROM block; omit entirely with ship_from_address when absent — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §26)",
    "ship_from_address": {
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string | null",
      "city": "string",
      "state": "string (2-letter code)",
      "zip": "string"
    },
    "invoice_no": "string",
    "invoice_date": "string (MM/DD/YYYY)",
    "supplier_account_no": "string",
    "espri_account_no": "string (omit when no override applies — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §14.4)",
    "original_invoice_no": "string | null",
    "bill_to_name": "string",
    "bill_to_address": {
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string | null",
      "city": "string",
      "state": "string (2-letter code)",
      "zip": "string"
    },
    "ship_to_name": "string",
    "ship_to_address": {
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string | null",
      "city": "string",
      "state": "string (2-letter code)",
      "zip": "string"
    },
    "order_no": "string | null",
    "terms": "string | null",
    "ship_via": "string | null",
    "comment": "string (text following a literal \"Comment:\" label anywhere on the document; omit entirely when not present — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §28)",
    "additional_header_fields": [{"label": "string — as printed on document", "value": "string — as printed on document"}, "omit entirely when none found — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §27"]
  },
  "line_items": [
    {
      "item_no": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "uom": "string",
      "qty": "number",
      "unit_price": "number",
      "line_amount": "number (negative)",
      "esprigas_item_no": "string — always empty string (\"\"); placeholder for EspriGas item# populated in a later step — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §13.4",
      "xref_source": "null (reserved for future cross-reference source tracking; always output null)"
    }
  ],
  "invoice_total": "number (negative)",
  "notes": "string | null"
}
]
```

---

## Confidence Scoring

See `confidence_scoring.md` for the full scoring rubric.

### Required Header Fields

| Field | Tier | Deduction |
|-------|------|----------:|
| `invoice_no` | 1 | −15 |
| `invoice_total` | 1 | −15 |
| `supplier_account_no` | 1 | −10 |
| `invoice_date` | 1 | −15 |

> **Tier 1 fields** also populate `required_fields_missing` when absent and flag the document for manual review — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §15.

### Integrity Checks

| Check | Condition | Deduction |
|-------|-----------|----------:|
| Line total reconciliation | `sum(line_amount) ≠ invoice_total` (both stored as negative numbers per the Amount Sign Convention above) | −25 |
| No line items | No line items extracted | −20 |
| Invalid invoice date | `invoice_date` cannot be parsed as a valid date | −10 |
| EspriGas direct delivery — customer unresolved | Ship-To Exclusion Rule applied (GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §1) to `ship_to_name` — no non-EspriGas/TMG customer name could be determined — flag `"(-20) esprigas_direct_delivery — non-EspriGas/TMG customer name could not be determined — manual review required"`. **Does not apply** when Ship-To Name Identification successfully resolved `ship_to_name` by stripping an EspriGas identifier — that is a correct extraction, not a defect, and carries no deduction. | −20 |

### Credit-Memo-Specific Deductions

| Condition | Deduction |
|-----------|-----------|
| `original_invoice_no` is null and document gives no cross-reference to the invoice being credited | −10 |
| Classification relied solely on negative total (no explicit credit memo label) | −10 |
| Any `line_amount` could not be unambiguously negated (ambiguous sign on source document) | −15 per affected line |

---

## Examples

### Invoice 308440 — Holston Gases / Lanesville Food Mart (-$22.00)

**Classification signals:** Invoice total is negative (-$22.00); description contains `"*** CREDIT MEMO ***"`.

**Header:**
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| vendor_name | Holston Gases |
| partner_name | Holston Gases |
| invoice_no | 308440 |
| supplier_account_no | B6046 |
| original_invoice_no | null *(not stated on document)* |
| invoice_total | -22.00 |

**Lines:**
| item_no | description | qty | unit_price | line_amount |
|---------|-------------|-----|------------|-------------|
| DELIVERY | Delivery Charges | -1 | 22.00 | -22.00 |

*Source document showed `"Delivery Charges *** CREDIT MEMO ***"` as the description — the `*** CREDIT MEMO ***` portion is a label, not part of the description. Amount was positive on source; stored as -22.00 per sign convention.*

---

## Vendor-Specific Notes

### Holston Gases
- Credit memos are formatted identically to standard Holston content invoices but carry a negative invoice total.
- The credit memo label `*** CREDIT MEMO ***` may appear inline within a line item description rather than in the document header.
- EspriGas Account: B6046.

# SOURCE: po_trade_partner_lookup_v1.3.md
---

# PO Trade Partner Reference — Extraction Lookup
**Version:** 1.3
**Model Target:** claude-sonnet-5-5
**Cache Strategy:** explicit
**Last Updated:** 2026-08-18
**Status:** Draft — mirrors invoice-side `trade_partner_lookup_v1.3.md` pattern, adapted for Purchase Orders.

---

## Purpose

Provides `trade_partner` code lookup at PO extraction time. Maps the buyer/ship-to name as printed on the Purchase Order to a normalized trade partner code. Applies to Purchase Order documents only — see `trade_partner_lookup_v1.3.md` for the invoice-side partner_name lookup.

---

## §PO-TP — Lookup Rule

1. Match the extracted `partner_name` (or ship-to name, if `partner_name` is not separately populated) against the "Vendor Name" column in §PO-TP.2, **case-insensitively**. Strip leading/trailing whitespace before matching.
2. If an exact match is found, populate `trade_partner` with the mapped code.
3. If no exact match, attempt a substring/partial match (e.g., a buyer name containing `"HOLSTON GASES-CLARKSVILLE"` matches that entry).
4. **Precedence with existing buyer-specific PO rules:** If a buyer-specific extraction rule already exists for this trade partner (see `purchase_order_extraction.md` Buyer-Specific PO Rules), the `trade_partner` code from **that** rule takes precedence over this table when the two conflict. Flag the conflict — see §PO-TP.1 below — rather than silently picking one.
5. If no match is found in either source, output `trade_partner: ""` (empty string). Do not leave the field entirely absent.
6. For buyers listed in §PO-TP.1 (known conflicts against existing buyer-specific rules): output the trade partner value from the **existing buyer-specific rule** (not this table), add flag `"trade_partner_conflict — manual review required"` to `confidence.flags`, and apply a −3 confidence deduction, consistent with the invoice-side handling in §TP.1.

---

## §PO-TP.1 — Known Conflicts (Flag and Defer to Existing Buyer-Specific Rule)

| Buyer (as printed) | This table says | Existing PO rule says | Resolution until confirmed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trane Technologies | `NNT_TRANE` | `TRANE` | Use `TRANE` (existing rule); flag conflict |
| Gensco / EspriGas - TMG Gases, Inc. / Slakey 1939 | `NNT_GENSCO` | `GENSCO` | Use `GENSCO` (existing rule); flag conflict |
| R.E. MICHEL | `NNT_RMICHEL` | `REMICHEL` | Use `REMICHEL` (existing rule); flag conflict — codes differ beyond the prefix |
| Locke Supply | `NNT_LOCSUPLY` | `LOCKESUPPLY` | Use `LOCKESUPPLY` (existing rule); flag conflict — codes differ beyond the prefix |
| American Refrigeration Supplies Inc. | `NNT_ARSORDER` | `ARS` | Use `ARS` (existing rule); flag conflict — codes differ beyond the prefix |

> **Note:** The existing buyer-specific PO rule code wins for these five, since it's tied to working extraction logic (e.g., REMICHEL's branch-number derivation, ARS's location-code and aluminum-suffix logic).
>
> **Scope of this table is deliberately narrow.** Since §PO-TP.2 adopted the BC `NNT_` prefix, the table value differs from the buyer-specific rule value for **all 23** buyers that have a dedicated rule — not only the five listed here. That divergence is expected and is **not** a conflict to flag (see the mixed-format note under §PO-TP.2). These five remain listed because their codes differ by more than the prefix alone, which is a genuine ambiguity. **Do not expand this table to cover prefix-only differences** — doing so would add a −3 deduction and a manual-review flag to nearly every Purchase Order.

---

## §PO-TP.2 — Buyer Name Lookup Table

Match `partner_name` (or ship-to name) from the PO header against the left column, case-insensitively.

> **These codes are transcribed from the Business Central database and are intentionally inconsistent. Do NOT normalize them.** The prefix casing varies by entry (`NNT_GENSCO` uppercase vs. `NNT_BehlerYoung` and `NNT_PeircePhelps` mixed-case), and some codes are not the spelling you would predict from the buyer name (`Locke Supply` → `NNT_LOCSUPLY`, not `NNT_LOCKESUPPLY`; `R.E. Michel` → `NNT_RMICHEL`, not `NNT_REMICHEL`). Each value must match BC exactly or the record fails at import. Do not "correct" casing, expand abbreviations, or align these with the codes used in `purchase_order_extraction.md`'s Buyer-Specific PO Rules — see the note below §PO-TP.2.

| Vendor Name (as printed) | trade_partner |
|---|---|
| Gensco | GENSCO |
| Pacden | PDS |
| C D Jones | CHARLESJONES |
| Carrier Enterprise LLC | CARRIERENTP |
| Chadwell Supply | CHADWELL |
| Dakota Supply | CALVERLEYS |
| Behler-Young | BehlerYoung |
| Baker Specialty & Supply Co. | BAKERSPE |

| Peirce-Phelps | PeircePhelps |
| Sid Harvey | SIDHARVEY |

| Tri-State | TRISTATE |
| Habegger | HABEGGER |
| Daikin | GOODMAN |
| Winsupply | WINSUPPLY |
| Sage Dental Management | SAGEDENT |

| Sanders Company | GEORGESANDER |
| Vamac | VAMAC |
| R.E. Michel | RMICHEL |

| Coburn Supply Company Inc. | COBURN |

| South Side | SOUTHSIDE |

> **Mixed-format output is expected and correct.** Per §PO-TP rule 4, a Buyer-Specific PO Rule takes precedence over this table. The 23 buyers with a dedicated rule in `purchase_order_extraction.md` therefore emit their **unprefixed** code (`TRANE`, `GENSCO`, `LOCKESUPPLY`, `ARS`, …), while buyers resolved only through this table emit the **`NNT_`-prefixed** code above. Both forms are valid BC values. Do not add the `NNT_` prefix to the Buyer-Specific PO Rules, and do not strip it here, in order to make the two agree.

## Open Items

1. ~~Resolve the five conflicts in §PO-TP.1 — confirm whether the existing buyer-specific codes should be renamed to match this table, or this table corrected to match them.~~ **RESOLVED 2026-08-18 — neither.** Both code sets stay exactly as recorded. The BC database itself carries these inconsistencies and the extraction output must match it, so the buyer-specific codes keep their unprefixed form and §PO-TP.2 keeps the `NNT_`-prefixed form, including its irregular casing and non-obvious spellings. Do not reopen this as a normalization task.
2. ~~Several buyers in §PO-TP.2 had no corresponding buyer-specific extraction rule and no fallback path to this table.~~ **RESOLVED 2026-08-03** — `purchase_order_extraction.md`'s `trade_partner` field rule and Buyer-Specific PO Rules section now explicitly fall back to this table (§PO-TP.2) for any buyer without a dedicated rule (C D Jones, Behler-Young, RSD - Lake Forest, Peirce-Phelps, Sid Harvey, Tri-State, Habegger, Epting Distributors, USACD Inc., 2J Supply, McCall's Supply Inc., Community Dental Partners).
3. Confirm whether this table should be embedded directly in `purchase_order_extraction.md` (matching how invoice-side inclusion works per the "Temporary model-layer inclusion" note in `trade_partner_lookup_v1.3.md`) or migrated straight to an external reference file.

# SOURCE: purchase_order_extraction_v1.34.md
---

# Purchase Order — Extraction Logic
**Version:** 1.34
**Model Target:** claude-sonnet-5-5
**Min Token Estimate:** ~4,350
**Cache Strategy:** explicit
**Last Updated:** 2026-09-16

---

## Purpose

Extracts structured data from Purchase Orders (POs) issued **by customers to EspriGas/TMG Gases** for gas products. The direction is the reverse of invoices — the buyer is EspriGas's customer; EspriGas is the seller/supplier.

**Key identifiers:** Header says `"PURCHASE ORDER"`. Has PO Number, Buyer name, line items with item number, description, qty, unit price.

**Multi-document / Mixed PDF handling:** A single file may contain multiple discrete documents. Classify each page independently per GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §7.4. When a Purchase Order is identified, treat it as a discrete document and produce a separate extraction output for each. Do not merge PO data with any other document type found in the same file.

**Important schema rule:** Purchase Orders must **never** populate `invoice_no`, `invoice_date`, or `invoice_total`. The primary document identifier is `po_number`. These are distinct document types with separate schemas.

---

## Extraction Rules

### PO Header Fields

| Field | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `po_number` | Buyer's PO number. May require concatenation with `external_no` — see below. |
| `po_date` | Date the PO was issued |
| `partner_name` | Name of the customer issuing the PO. **CSV/flat-file input with no vendor-name column: apply §3.11** — use the same value resolved for `trade_partner` below. |
| `trade_partner` | **CSV/flat-file input: check §3.10 first** — if the file has a `TradePartner` column, use its value directly (Priority 1); else if the filename carries a `<TradePartner>_` prefix, use that value directly (Priority 2); either way, skip the resolution order below. Otherwise, BC trade partner code for the buyer resolved in this order: (1) if a Buyer-Specific PO Rule below names this buyer, use the `trade_partner` value from that rule; (2) otherwise, look up `partner_name` (or ship-to name) in `po_trade_partner_lookup.md` §PO-TP.2, case-insensitively, per the §PO-TP lookup rule (including its §PO-TP.1 conflict handling); (3) if neither resolves a value, output `trade_partner: ""`. Also validated and enriched via post-processing reference table. See `post_processing/trade_partner_reference.md`. |
| `customer_address` | Address where EspriGas should deliver the goods — split into `address_1`, `address_2`, `city`, `state`, `zip` |
| `external_no` | Secondary reference number; sometimes appended to po_number — see below |
| `payment_terms` | Payment terms if stated |
| `revision` | PO revision number if stated |
| `customer_po_number` | End-customer's own PO number, when the document names a separate end customer distinct from the buyer. When no separate end-customer PO is stated, defaults to the same value as `po_number` — see below. |
| `order_no` | Vendor's or buyer's internal order reference |
| `supplier_account_no` | Never populated on Purchase Orders — see below. |
| `po_total` | Total order amount if stated on the document |
| `comment` | Free-text notes field. Populated from a printed PO Note / Special Instructions field and/or the Special-Handling Keyword Flag — see "PO Notes and Special-Handling Keyword Flag" below. `null` when neither source produces a value. |
| `document_comment` | **Distinct from `comment` above.** Text following a literal `Comment:` label anywhere on the document — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §28. Named `document_comment` on Purchase Orders specifically because `comment` was already taken by the PO Notes/Special Instructions field above; every other document type calls this field `comment`. Omit entirely when no `Comment:` label is present; do not conflate with the PO Note/Special Instructions text that populates `comment`. |
| `is_rush` | Boolean. Whether the buyer marked the order as expedited — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §23.2. Always populated (`true`/`false`), never omitted. |

### `po_number` — Label-Anchored Extraction

Extract `po_number` from the value printed under its own explicit label — `"Purchase Order Number"` (or an equivalent, e.g. `"PO Number"`, `"P.O. Number"`) — as it appears in the document's visual layout. Do not rely on raw text-extraction order or position (e.g., "the first value beneath the document title") to identify it.

Some PO templates place other header values out of sequence in the underlying text layer relative to their own labels — most notably the `"External PO Number"` field's value, which can appear positioned before its own label, sometimes directly beneath the main document title, ahead of where `"Purchase Order Number"` and its value print. If extraction follows raw text order rather than each value's true printed label, this can result in the `"External PO Number"` value being written to `po_number` instead of the correct value. Always confirm `po_number` against its own printed label — `"Purchase Order Number"` — before writing output; never substitute a nearby or out-of-sequence value, and never use the `"External PO Number"` value for `po_number` under any circumstance.

### `supplier_account_no` — Not Used on Purchase Orders

`supplier_account_no` is never populated on Purchase Orders — leave it absent, regardless of what label the value sits under on the document (`"Account No."`, `"Account #"`, `"Customer Account"`, `"Supplier ID"`, `"Vendor Account"`, or unlabeled). This field is for Supplier Invoices only, where it captures EspriGas's own account number with that supplier; on a PO, any comparable-looking number is the buyer's own internal AP/vendor-master filing code for EspriGas — it never carries a meaning EspriGas can use, whether or not the buyer happens to print a label on it. See "Fields never used on Purchase Orders" below.

### `customer_po_number` — Default to `po_number`

`customer_po_number` must never be written as an empty string when a `po_number` value exists. `customer_po_number` is a normal required string field with no "omit if unresolved" allowance — it always carries a value, one way or another.

Determine the value in this order:

1. Check whether the document names a separate end customer distinct from the buyer issuing the PO (the buyer is placing the order on that customer's behalf) **and** prints a distinct PO reference for that end customer. If so, use that printed value.
2. Otherwise — no separate end customer is named, or one is named but no distinct PO reference is printed for them — **set `customer_po_number` equal to the extracted `po_number` value.** This is a required assignment, not an optional fallback: do not leave the field blank, do not write an empty string, and do not treat "no separate end-customer PO" as a reason to leave the field unresolved.

### Account Selection — Multiple Candidates

When a verified account number cannot be read directly from the document and a lookup by supplier + ship-to returns more than one candidate, use the `Account Status` field on each candidate to select the correct account:

| Scenario | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Exactly one candidate has `Account Status = Primary` | Select that account number automatically |
| No Primary candidates; exactly one candidate has `Account Status = Backup` | Select that Backup account number automatically |
| No Primary candidates; two or more candidates have `Account Status = Backup` | Flag document for **manual review** — do not select automatically |

> **Data availability note:** The account candidate database that supplies `Account Status` values is not yet available. This rule will take effect once access is provided. Until then, treat all unresolved multi-candidate account numbers as requiring manual review.

### PO Number Concatenation

Some POs include a separate release or external reference number (`external_no_temp`) that must be appended to the base PO number:

```
Final PO Number = po_number + "-" + external_no_temp
```

Apply only when `external_no_temp` is present and non-empty on the document.

### Quantity Derivation — General Rule

When `Quantity` is absent or blank but `Line_Amount` and `Price` are both present:

```
Quantity = int(round(Line_Amount / Price, 2))
```

Always round to 2 decimal places before truncating to integer. If both `Line_Amount` and `Price` are 0.00 and Quantity is blank, default `Quantity = 1`.

### Line Amount Derivation — General Rule

When `Line_Amount` is absent or blank but `Quantity` and `Price` are both present:

```
Line_Amount = round(Quantity * Price, 2)
```

Verify all lines after derivation: `Quantity × Price = Line_Amount`.

### Item No — Source Column

`item_no` is sourced from the PO line-item table column headed (case-insensitive) `"Item No"` (also match `"Item Number"`, `"Item ID"`, `"Stock Number"` / `"Stock No"` / `"Stock #"`, `"Our Number"` / `"Our No."` / `"Our Part #"`, and `"Product"` / `"Product and Description"` as the same field) — extract the cell value verbatim. `"Product"` / `"Product and Description"` is a distinct, valid source column and is not affected by the `"Product No"` retirement below. When this column combines the code and description in one cell (code on the first line, description text on the line(s) below, with no separate description column), extract only the first line as `item_no`. This is a straight swap from the prior source column, `"Product No"` — do not match `"Product No"`; if a PO prints `"Product No"` only (no `"Item No"` / `"Item Number"` / `"Item ID"` / `"Stock Number"` / `"Our Number"` / `"Product"` column) and no Buyer-Specific PO Rule applies, `item_no` is absent per standard missing-field handling, with no fallback to `"Product No"`.

**Stacked/multi-line column headers:** Some vendors print a single compound header made of several stacked labels within one header cell (e.g., `"Supplier Part No"` / `"Item ID"` / `"Item Description"` printed as three lines), with each line item's cell echoing the same stacked order. When this pattern appears, match each stacked sub-label independently against the labels above and extract only the stacked line within the cell that corresponds to the matched sub-label — not the first line by default, and not the full cell. `"Supplier Part No"` is a distinct field from `"Item No"` / `"Item Number"` / `"Item ID"` and is never used as `item_no` unless a Buyer-Specific PO Rule says otherwise.

**The match is positional, not by a repeated label.** Only the header cell states the stacked sub-labels (once, at the top of the column); each line item's cell echoes the *values* in that same top-to-bottom order without restating the label text — the row itself will never contain the literal words `"Item ID"`. Do not search each row for an inline label to confirm which line is which, and do not conclude the field is absent just because no such label is repeated on the row — that is the expected, normal shape of this pattern, not a missing-data case. Identify the sub-label's position in the header (e.g., `"Item ID"` is the 2nd of 3 stacked labels), then take the line at that same position in the cell (the 2nd line), regardless of whether further lines follow it (a description continuation, a secondary note, or a blank spacer line beneath the third sub-label does not shift or invalidate the position of the lines above it). Example: a cell reading `"PR33"` / `"1SPROPANE"` / `"PROPANE, CONTENTS ONLY"` — with further description text continuing below — still yields `item_no: "1SPROPANE"` from position 2; it must never be extracted as blank/absent.

**Placeholder line followed by the real value:** Some product-code cells print a placeholder token on their first line — e.g. `"**None**"`, `"NONE"`, `"N/A"` — with the actual code appearing on a second line within the same cell (e.g. a `"Stock Number"` cell reading `"**None**"` on line one and `"00633025453"` on line two). Do not treat the placeholder line as the field's true value, and do not conclude the field is absent without checking the rest of the cell. When a second line in the same cell holds a real alphanumeric value, use that value for `item_no`; only fall back to standard missing-field handling when no non-placeholder line is present in the cell at all.

**Customer/vendor part numbers — always `item_no`, never a direct copy into `esprigas_item_no`:** Some POs print two distinct codes per line: one under a column headed `"Item No"` / `"Item Number"` / `"Item ID"` (the buyer's own item code) and a second column separately labeled as the manufacturer's or vendor's own number (e.g. `"Manufacturer Number"`, `"Manuf#"`, `"Mfg #"`, `"Mfr Number"`, `"Vend-Part#"`, `"Vendor Part #"`, `"Vendor P/N"` — sometimes introduced inline by a marker such as `"Manuf# -->"` rather than a column header). Extract only the buyer's own item column as `item_no`; the second, manufacturer/vendor-labeled column is not extracted into any field — not `item_no`, and not `esprigas_item_no` — ignore it entirely. Do not reason that "EspriGas is the manufacturer, so this column is our number" as a basis for writing it anywhere; a value printed on the customer's PO is never written directly into `esprigas_item_no`, regardless of which column it came from.

**Single item-code column:** When a PO prints only one item-code value per line, that value is always extracted as `item_no` — even when it happens to numerically match the EspriGas `esprigas_item_no` scheme (§13.8) or a known cross-reference entry. Never divert a single printed value to `esprigas_item_no` in place of `item_no`, and never conclude `item_no` is absent merely because the printed value happens to decode as a valid EspriGas item code.

**`esprigas_item_no` is never a direct copy of a printed PO value.** Whether a PO shows one item column or two, `esprigas_item_no` is populated only by the independent Step 1–5 resolution algorithm (§13.4) — Fee/Resource Mapping, Bulk Gas Product Mapping, Cross-Reference Lookup against the extracted `item_no`, or §13.8 scheme construction — never by copying a customer- or vendor-printed value straight across. It is expected and correct for `item_no` and `esprigas_item_no` to end up holding the same value when that independent resolution happens to match the vendor's own numbering — but the match must come from running the algorithm, not from treating a printed column as already-resolved.

Existing Buyer-Specific PO Rules that derive `item_no` by their own logic (e.g., VAMAC's positional extraction, JOHNSTONE's fixed-priority extraction, LENNOX's first-word rule) are unaffected — those rules do not read from a header-labeled column and take precedence as documented below.

### Item No Normalization

After extraction or derivation by any method, apply in order: (1) remove the substrings `ESPRIGAS`, `ESPRI`, and `USP` (in that order — longest first to prevent partial matches); (2) remove all spaces.

### PO Notes and Special-Handling Keyword Flag

`comment` is populated from two independent sources, combined when both apply.

**1. Printed PO Note / Special Instructions.** When the document carries an explicitly labeled free-text field — e.g. `"PO Note:"`, `"PO Notes:"`, `"Special Instructions"`, `"Shipping Instructions"`, `"Notes:"` — extract its text verbatim, trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace. This includes a boxed/bordered free-text field printed within the line-item table area itself (not just the document header) — a bordered box labeled `"SHIPPING INSTRUCTIONS"` sitting above the line rows is this same field, not a line item.

**2. Special-Handling Keyword Flag.** Applies to **every** Purchase Order, regardless of buyer. After extracting all lines, scan the full document — every line item description, any printed PO Note / Special Instructions text (source 1 above), and any other free-text header field — case-insensitively for the following trigger words:

- `LEAKER`
- `EMPTY`
- `WARRANTY`
- `ALUMINUM`

If one or more trigger words are found anywhere, produce a short note listing which word(s) matched, e.g. `"Contains reference to: LEAKER"` or `"Contains reference to: WARRANTY, ALUMINUM"` when more than one trigger word appears. List each matched word once, in the order first encountered — do not repeat a word for multiple occurrences.

**Combining the two sources.** When both a printed note (source 1) and a keyword match (source 2) are present, write both to `comment`, separated by ` | ` — the printed note text first, then the keyword note, e.g. `"Full tanks With exchanges. | Contains reference to: WARRANTY"`. When only one source produces a value, write that value alone. When neither source produces a value, `comment` is `null` — do not write an empty string or omit the field.

This remains an informational field only — it does not affect `confidence.score` and does not add a `confidence.flags` entry. It exists so a reviewer can immediately see a buyer's printed note or a special-handling signal (a leaker/empty-cylinder return, a warranty claim, an aluminum-specific item) without reading every line description in the detail view.

---

## Buyer-Specific PO Rules

The buyers below each have a documented extraction override. **For any buyer not listed here** (e.g., C D Jones, Behler-Young, RSD - Lake Forest, Peirce-Phelps, Sid Harvey, Tri-State, Habegger, Epting Distributors, USACD Inc., 2J Supply, McCall's Supply Inc., Community Dental Partners), do not leave `trade_partner` unresolved — look it up in `po_trade_partner_lookup.md` §PO-TP.2 per the field rule above, and apply only the General Extraction Rules (Quantity/Line Amount Derivation, Item No Normalization) above for the rest of the line.

### TRANE TECHNOLOGIES (`trade_partner = "TRANE"`)

- **Account number / external_no derivation:** Derived from the ship-to address string.
  - Strip all non-alphanumeric characters from the ship-to address.
  - Take the first 8 characters of the result.
  - Use as `external_no`.
  - Example: `"8715 Owenfield Drive"` → strip → `"8715OwenfieldDrive"` → first 8 → `"8715Owen"`

### COBURN (`trade_partner = "COBURN"`)

- **Line Amount not printed:** Derive: `Line_Amount = round(Price × Quantity, 2)`
- **Negative quantity rows:** Exclude. These represent cancelled or reversed order lines.
- **Item no:** All COBURN lines use item number `"710013"`.
- **MEMO row removal:** Exclude any line where Description contains `"MEMO"`.

### GENSCO (`trade_partner = "GENSCO"`)

- **Quantity not printed:** Derive: `Quantity = int(round(Line_Amount / Price, 2))`

### JOHNSTONE (`trade_partner = "JOHNSTONE"`, `partner_name = "Johnstone Supply"`)

- **Quantity derivation:** `Quantity = int(round(Line_Amount / Price, 2))`. If both are 0.00 and Quantity is blank, default to 1.
- **Item No derivation** — priority order:
  1. If description contains `"ALUMINUM"` (case-insensitive): append `"-A"` to the full description string → `item_no`.
  2. Otherwise, split description into words. If the **last word is numeric** (digits only): use that number as `item_no`.
  3. If neither: use the full description string as `item_no`.
  - Apply standard Item No Normalization (strip `ESPRIGAS`/`ESPRI`/`USP`, remove spaces) to the result of any branch, same as every other PO line.
  - **Examples:**
    - `"COPPER TUBE TYPE L ALUMINUM 1/2"` → contains ALUMINUM → `"COPPER TUBE TYPE L ALUMINUM 1/2-A"`
    - `"FILTER DRIER 12345"` → last word numeric → `"12345"`
    - `"FLEX DUCT R8"` → neither → `"FLEX DUCT R8"`
- **Negative quantity rows:** Exclude after derivation.

### VAMAC (`trade_partner = "VAMAC"`)

- **Quantity not printed:** Derive: `Quantity = int(round(Line_Amount / Price, 2))`
- **Item no derivation (positional):** The item number is embedded mid-description at a known offset:
  - If description length > 27 characters: item number = characters at positions 21–27 (inclusive)
  - If description length ≤ 27 characters: item number = characters at positions 17–22 (inclusive)
  - If extracted value equals `"(GAS"` (OCR artifact): re-apply derivation above
  - If result appears garbled: fall back to the first word of the description

### SHEARER (`trade_partner = "SHEARER"`)

- **Quantity not printed:** `Quantity = int(round(Line_Amount / Price, 2))`. On division error (Price = 0), default `Quantity = 0`.

### CARRIERENTP (`trade_partner = "CARRIERENTP"`, `partner_name = "KILLEEN"` or `"CARRIER"`)

- **Quantity derivation:** `Quantity = int(round(Line_Amount / Price, 2))`
- Both buyer names (`"KILLEEN"` and `"CARRIER"`) map to trade partner `"CARRIERENTP"`.
- **Sparse table filtering:** Discard any table with 4 or fewer distinct column labels.

### BAKERSPE (`trade_partner = "BAKERSPE"`, `partner_name = "BAKER"`)

- **Negative quantity rows:** Exclude. Do not attempt to derive quantity — use the value as printed.

### GOODMAN (`trade_partner = "GOODMAN"`, `partner_name = "DAIKIN"`)

- **Price column absent:** If no Price column, the Line_Amount column contains the unit price. Extract as Price, then recalculate: `Line_Amount = round(Price × Quantity, 2)`
- **Price cell blank:** Default `Price = "357"` (Nanonets-era placeholder — confirm with EspriGas whether this maps to a real BC item number or should remain blank).
- **Line Amount blank:** If blank but Price and Quantity populated: `Line_Amount = round(Price × Quantity, 2)`
- **`po_number` — strip leading zeros:** Daikin PO numbers sometimes print with one or more leading zeros (e.g. `"0004469647"`). Strip all leading zeros before writing `po_number` — e.g. `"0004469647"` → `"4469647"`. Apply this to the base `po_number` as printed, before PO Number Concatenation (above) if `external_no_temp` also applies. If stripping leading zeros would leave an empty string (a PO number of all zeros), retain a single `"0"` rather than outputting an empty value.

### CHADWELL (`trade_partner = "CHADWELL"`, `partner_name = "Chadwell SUPPLY"`)

- **Dollar signs in price fields:** Strip all `$` characters from Price and Line_Amount values before extracting.

### SAGEDENT (`trade_partner = "SAGEDENT"`, `partner_name = "Sage Dental"`)

- **Dollar signs in price fields:** Strip all `$` characters from Price and Line_Amount values.

### ECONOMICELEC (`trade_partner = "ECONOMICELEC"`)

- **Dollar signs in price fields:** Strip all `$` characters from Price and Line_Amount values.
- **Quantity derivation:** `Quantity = round(Line_Amount / Price, 2)` — keep decimal (not truncated to integer).

### WINSUPPLY (`trade_partner = "WINSUPPLY"`)

- **Item no derivation:** Take the first 19 characters of Description, strip whitespace, replace ` - ` (space-dash-space) with `-` (dash only).
- **Item no blank:** If Item_No column is present but cell is blank, use `"357"` as placeholder.
- **Line Amount blank:** If blank but Price and Quantity present: `Line_Amount = round(Price × Quantity, 2)`

### ROGERSUPPLY (`trade_partner = "ROGERSUPPLY"`)

- **Item no is always fixed:** Regardless of what appears on the PO, item number for all lines is `"95313"`. This is a catch-all code — all Roger Supply PO lines map to a single EspriGas product.

### LACKLAND (`trade_partner = "LACKLAND"`)

- **Price not printed:** If Price cell is blank, default `Price = "1"`.
- **Line Amount not printed:** If Line_Amount cell is blank, default `Line_Amount = "1"`.
- These defaults exist so the line passes validation; the actual value is the quantity field.

### CALVERLEYS (`trade_partner = "CALVERLEYS"`, `partner_name = "Dakota"`)

- **Item no derivation:** Take the first 7 characters of Description, stripped.
  - Example: `"T0170AL Aluminum Co2 Refill Gas"` → `"T0170AL"`
- **Item no blank:** If Item_No column is present but cell is blank, use `"357"`.

### LOCKESUPPLY (`trade_partner = "LOCKESUPPLY"`, `partner_name = "901 LOCKE SUPPLY"`)

- **Item no derivation:** Take the first 21 characters of Description, stripped.
- **Item no blank:** If Item_No column is present but cell is blank, use `"Espri"` as placeholder.

### SOUTHSIDE (`trade_partner = "SOUTHSIDE"`)

- **Item no derivation:** Take the first word of Description (split on spaces). Strip any `*` characters.
- If Item_No column exists but is blank: apply derivation above; do not leave blank.

### LENNOX (`trade_partner = "LENNOX"`, `partner_name = "Lennox"`)

- **Item no derivation:** Take the first word of Description. Strip any `*` characters.
- **Override:** `"Nitrogen 60 Refill"` → item number = `"211060"` (not the first word).

### STANDARDS (`trade_partner = "STANDARDS"`, `partner_name = "Standards"`)

- **Item no derivation:** Take the first word of Description. Strip any `*` characters.
- **Known overrides:**
  - `"NITROGEN REFILL 40 CU. FT."` → `"211040"`
  - `"OXYGEN REFILL GAS 20 CU. FT."` → `"111020"`
  - `"ACETYLENE REFILL 10 CU. FT."` → `"311010"`

### PDS (`trade_partner = "PDS"`)

- **Quantity derivation:** `Quantity = round(Line_Amount / Price, 2)` — keep decimal (not truncated). Both blank and non-blank Quantity cells are overwritten with the derived value.
- **Multi-page table continuation:** PDS POs sometimes split a single line item across page boundaries.
  - **Detection:** If the last two rows on a page share the same `Quantity` **or** the same `Line_Amount`, the actual last row is a continuation stub.
  - **Resolution:**
    1. Look at the first row of the next page.
    2. If that page has exactly one row with Quantity and Line_Amount columns, use those values to complete the last row of the current page.
    3. Discard the first row of the next page after transferring its values.
    4. If the next page's first table is empty after removal, discard the table entirely.

### ARS (`trade_partner = "ARS"`)

- **Location code as external_no:** The Ship To name field includes a location code in the format `S##`. Extract the alphanumeric code immediately following `ARS ` and before the ` - ` separator.
  - Pattern: `ARS <CODE> - <LOCATION NAME>` → `external_no = <CODE>`
  - Example: `"ARS S07 - SCOTTSDALE"` → `external_no = "S07"`
- **Aluminum cylinder suffix:** When a line item description contains `"ALUMINUM"` (case-insensitive), append `"A"` to the base Part No. and `esprigas_item_no`.
  - Pattern: base Part No. + `"A"` → e.g., `511020` + `"A"` = `511020A`
  - This refers to cylinder material (aluminum vs. steel), not a gas type.

### REMICHEL (`trade_partner = "REMICHEL"`)

- **Branch number as external_no:** The Ship To name field includes a branch number in the format `#NN` or `#NNN`.
  - Pattern: `R.E. Michel Company #<N>` → `external_no = zero-pad(<N>, 3 digits)`
  - Examples:
    - `R.E. Michel Company #46` → `external_no = "046"`
    - `R.E. Michel Company #7` → `external_no = "007"`
    - `R.E. Michel Company #123` → `external_no = "123"`
  - The `External PO Number` field printed on the document header is separate and may be blank. Do not confuse it with this branch-derived `external_no`.

## Output Schema

**Output format:** Always return a JSON array — one element per extracted document. See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §16.

```json
[
{
  "document_type": "purchase_order",
  "source_file_output_total": "integer — total output records expected from this source file (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §7.9)",
  "source_page_start": "integer — 1-indexed page number where this document begins in the source PDF/image; omit for CSV/flat-file input (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §7.10)",
  "source_rows": ["integer — 1-indexed file line numbers (header = line 1) contributing to this document; omit for PDF/image input (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §3.9)"],
  "required_fields_missing": ["string — Tier 1 field names absent from source document; omit this field entirely when all Tier 1 fields are present (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §15)"],
  "rosetta_version": "string (vX.XX — Rosetta Combined version used for this extraction)",
  "confidence": {
    "score": "integer (0–100)",
    "label": "HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW",
    "flags": ["string"]
  },
  "header": {
    "po_number": "string",
    "po_date": "string (MM/DD/YYYY)",
    "partner_name": "string",
    "trade_partner": "string",
    "customer_address": {
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string | null",
      "city": "string",
      "state": "string (2-letter code)",
      "zip": "string"
    },
    "external_no": "string",
    "payment_terms": "string",
    "revision": "string",
    "customer_po_number": "string",
    "order_no": "string",
    "espri_account_no": "string (omit when no override applies — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §14.4)",
    "po_total": "number | null",
    "comment": "string | null — printed PO Note/Special Instructions text and/or the Special-Handling Keyword Flag (LEAKER/EMPTY/WARRANTY/ALUMINUM), combined per \"PO Notes and Special-Handling Keyword Flag\"; null when neither is present",
    "document_comment": "string (distinct from comment above — text following a literal \"Comment:\" label anywhere on the document; omit entirely when not present — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §28)",
    "is_rush": "boolean — true when the order was marked expedited (GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §23.2); always populated, never omitted"
  },
  "lines": [
    {
      "line_no": "string",
      "item_no": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "quantity": "number",
      "uom": "string | null",
      "price": "number",
      "line_amount": "number",
      "tanks_to_pickup": "number | null",
      "esprigas_item_no": "string — resolved via the GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §13.4 Step 1–5 algorithm; omit this key entirely when unresolved (never an empty string, never a direct copy of a printed PO value — see \"esprigas_item_no is never a direct copy of a printed PO value\" above)",
      "xref_source": "null (reserved for future cross-reference source tracking; always output null)"
    }
  ]
}
]
```

**Fields never used on Purchase Orders:** `invoice_no`, `invoice_date`, `invoice_total`, `supplier_account_no` — omit these entirely.

---

## Examples

### PO 4503245646 — Lennox Industries / TMG Gases

**Header:**
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| po_number | 4503245646 |
| partner_name | Lennox Industries |
| trade_partner | LENNOX |

**Line pattern:**
| item_no | description | quantity | price | line_amount |
|-------------|-------------|----------|-------|-------------|
| (first word of description) | [gas product description] | [qty] | [price] | [qty × price] |

*Note: For Lennox, item number = first word of description, with override for `"Nitrogen 60 Refill"` → `"211060"`.*

---

## Confidence Scoring

See `confidence_scoring.md` for the shared scoring model, output format, and application steps.

### Required Header Fields

| Field | Tier | Deduction |
|-------|------|----------:|
| `po_number` | 1 | −20 |
| `partner_name` | 1 | −15 |
| `trade_partner` | 1 | −15 |
| `po_date` | 2 | −10 |
| `customer_address` | 3 | −5 |

> **Tier 1 fields** also populate `required_fields_missing` when absent and flag the document for manual review — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §15.

### Integrity Checks

| Check | Condition | Deduction |
|-------|-----------|----------:|
| No product lines | No line items extracted | −15 |
| Line math validation | `quantity × price ≠ line_amount` on any line | −15 |
| Invalid PO date | `po_date` cannot be parsed as a valid date | −10 |

### Minor Flags

| Check | Condition | Deduction |
|-------|-----------|----------:|
| Missing optional field | `payment_terms`, `revision`, or `external_no` absent | −2 per field |

# SOURCE: supplier_statement_extraction_v1.19.md
---

# Supplier Statement — Extraction Logic
**Version:** 1.19
**Model Target:** claude-sonnet-5-5
**Min Token Estimate:** ~2,885
**Cache Strategy:** explicit
**Last Updated:** 2026-09-10

---

## Purpose

Extracts structured data from vendor Supplier Statements submitted to EspriGas. Statements are account-level summaries listing open invoices and payments. They are **not invoices** — they contain no product line detail.

**Key identifiers:** Header says `"STATEMENT"`. Has columns for INVOICE DATE, INVOICE NUMBER, DOC TYPE, SUMMARY OF CHARGES, SUMMARY OF PAYMENTS, BALANCE DUE.

**Multi-document / Mixed PDF handling:** A single file may contain multiple discrete documents — for example, a Rental Invoice on page 1 and a Statement on page 2. Classify each page independently per GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §7.4. When a Statement is identified, treat it as a discrete document and produce a separate extraction output. Do not merge Statement data with any invoice data from the same file.

**Important:** Statements are marked `extractable: false` and described in the `notes` field only when they contain no actionable invoice rows. When a statement is the only document in a file, extract header-level information (vendor, account, statement date, total balance) and list invoice references in `notes`. Do not create product line items from a statement.

---

## Extraction Rules

### Bill-To Context

Statements list EspriGas's open balance with a vendor. The `supplier_account_no` is EspriGas's account number with the vendor. The customer name printed on the statement is **not always a fixed value** (e.g. not always `"TMG GASES, INC."`) — the same real-world EspriGas entity appears under different registered names or DBAs depending on which vendor account was set up (`TMG Gases, Inc.`, `EspriGas`, `Esprigas - CCBCC`, etc.). See Sold To — Customer Block below for the extraction rule; never hardcode or assume a fixed customer name.

### Sold To — Customer Block

**Always extract `sold_to` from the "Bill To" / "Customer" block on the statement — never hardcode or assume a fixed value.** Label wording varies by vendor template — match on intent (which block identifies who is being billed / who owes this money) rather than exact label text. Look for a block labeled with any of the following:

- `BILL TO` / `Bill To` / `B I L L T O` (often stacked vertically in a boxed column)
- `CUSTOMER`
- `SOLD TO`
- `MAIL TO` (only if no other Bill To/Customer block exists — verify it refers to the customer, not the vendor's own remittance address)

The **first line of text inside that block** is the `sold_to` value. Copy it **verbatim**, including any suffixes such as `- CCBCC`, `dba ...`, abbreviations, etc. — do not normalize or pick one variant as "the" correct name.

| Statement | Label used on form | `sold_to` value extracted |
|---|---|---|
| Youngstown Oxygen & Welding Supply | `CUSTOMER` | `TMG GASES, INC.` |
| CO2Meter, Inc. | `Bill To` | `EspriGas` |
| Young Welding Supply, Inc. | `B I L L T O` | `Esprigas - CCBCC` |
| Blue Water Industrial Products | `B I L L T O` | `TMG GASES, INC.` |

**`sold_to_address`:** Extract the address lines immediately following the `sold_to` name in the same block — split into `address_1`, `address_2` (`null` if no second line — only split a suite/unit out to `address_2` when it appears on its own line, otherwise leave it inline with `address_1`), `city`, `state`, `zip`.

**Treat each statement independently** — don't cross-reference or "correct" one statement's `sold_to` using another statement's value; different vendors may legitimately use different names/DBAs for the same real-world customer.

### Account Selection — Multiple Candidates

When a verified account number cannot be read directly from the document and a lookup by supplier + ship-to returns more than one candidate, use the `Account Status` field on each candidate to select the correct account:

| Scenario | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Exactly one candidate has `Account Status = Primary` | Select that account number automatically |
| No Primary candidates; exactly one candidate has `Account Status = Backup` | Select that Backup account number automatically |
| No Primary candidates; two or more candidates have `Account Status = Backup` | Flag document for **manual review** — do not select automatically |

> **Data availability note:** The account candidate database that supplies `Account Status` values is not yet available. This rule will take effect once access is provided. Until then, treat all unresolved multi-candidate account numbers as requiring manual review.

### Statement Header Fields

| Field | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `supplier_account_no` | The customer's account/customer number with that specific vendor — vendor-assigned, not universal. Common labels: `CUST. NO.`, `CUSTOMER NUMBER`, `ACCOUNT NUMBER`, or a bare numeric code repeated near the remittance/mail-to section. If the field is blank on the Bill-To/Customer block but the same number appears elsewhere on the page (e.g. repeated in a remittance stub or mailing area), use that repeated number. `null` if no such number is printed anywhere on the statement. |
| `sold_to` | See Sold To — Customer Block above. |
| `sold_to_address` | See Sold To — Customer Block above. |
| `statement_date` | Date of the statement. Normalize to `MM/DD/YYYY` regardless of source format (e.g. `08/31/25` → `08/31/2025`). Default to today's date when absent for vendors that require it. |
| `vendor_name` | Name of the issuing vendor, from its own letterhead/logo area (top-left or top-center) — the company issuing the statement, not the customer. |
| `partner_name` | Supplier name as printed on the statement, extracted verbatim per GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §2. Holds the **same supplier name** as `vendor_name` — populate **both** fields; neither substitutes for the other. `partner_name` is the canonical field for Trade Partner matching and for consistency with the invoice document types. Distinct from `supplier_name` below, which is the remit-to payee and may differ. |
| `supplier_name` / `supplier_address` | The vendor's remit-to entity name and address — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §19. Omit both entirely when neither a remit-to block nor a general vendor address appears on the document. |
| `trade_partner` / `parent_vendor_no` | Look up `partner_name` (or `vendor_name`) against the Account Name column in the Trade Partner Reference table's §TP.3 (`trade_partner_lookup.md`), case-insensitively, per that table's Matching Rules. If a match is found and it is not one of the §TP.3 Ambiguous Names, populate both fields from that row. If the Account Name matches an Ambiguous Names entry, flag the document for manual review per §TP.3 rule 4 rather than auto-assigning either field. If no match is found, output `trade_partner: ""` and omit `parent_vendor_no` entirely. |
| `comment` | Text following a literal `Comment:` label anywhere on the statement — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §28. Omit entirely when no `Comment:` label is present. |

### Statement Line Fields

| Field | Label | Notes |
|-------|-------|-------|
| `invoice_no` | Invoice_No | Individual invoice numbers listed |
| `doc_date` | Doc_Date | Date of each listed invoice |
| `type` | Type / Category | Transaction type: invoice, payment, finance charge, credit memo, etc. |
| `inv_amt` | Inv_Amt | Invoice amount per row; may require derivation (see below) |
| `open_amt` | Open_Amt | Open balance; some vendors use this instead of Inv_Amt |
| `supplier_account_no` | supplier_account_no | EspriGas's account; propagate from first row when blank on subsequent rows |

### Row Filtering — What to Exclude

Keep **only rows that represent outstanding invoices**. Exclude rows where the `Type` or `Category` field contains any of the following (case-insensitive):

| Pattern | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| `"PAYMENT"`, `"Payment"` | Payment applied to account |
| `"Finance Charge"`, `"FIN CHRG"`, `"FINANCE CHARGES"`, `"FC"` | Finance/late charges |
| `"CRD MEMO"`, `"CR MEMO"`, `"CRMEMO"` | Credit memo |
| `"UNAPPLIED CASH"`, `"UNCASH"`, `"UN CASH"` | Unapplied cash payment |
| `"Balance Forward"` | Carried-forward balance row |
| `"Late Charges"`, `"ADJUSTMENT"` | Adjustment rows |
| `"Service Charge"`, `"SERVICE CHARGE"`, `"SERVICECHARGE"` | Service charges |
| `"ACH PAYMENT"` | Electronic payment |

Also exclude rows where:
- `invoice_no` contains `"-PP"` (pre-payment reference)
- `invoice_no` contains `"PMT"` or `"FC"`
- `invoice_no` = `"ENDING BALANCE"`
- `invoice_no` matches only zeros or a single digit (e.g., `"0"`, `"00001"`) — placeholder rows
- `invoice_no` = `"88888888"` (known dummy value)
- `inv_amt` is blank or empty (unless derivation applies below)
- `inv_amt` contains `"CR"` (credit indicator)
- `inv_amt` is negative
- `type` = `"U"`, `"C"`, `"DD"`, `"T"`, `"PY"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, `"4"` (payment/credit/adjustment type codes)

After filtering, keep only rows that still have an `invoice_no` field present.

### Inv_Amt Derivation — Filling Blank Amounts

Many vendor statements omit the invoice amount from `inv_amt` but include it in an `Adjustments` field. When `inv_amt` is blank (or equals `".00"`, `"00"`, or `"100"` — known Nanonets OCR artifacts for a blank field):

1. Check `Adjustments`, `Adjustments1`, `Adjustments2`, `Adjustments3` in order.
2. Use the first field that has a non-zero, non-blank value.
3. Set `inv_amt` to that value.

If no Adjustments field has a value but a `Credit` field is present and non-blank:
- Set `inv_amt = "-" + credit_value` (credit amounts become negative invoice amounts).

If `inv_amt` is still blank after both checks, exclude the row.

### Sparse Table Removal

Discard any table that has 3 or fewer distinct column labels. These are page-level headers or totals rows that OCR picked up as a table but contain no invoice detail.

### Date Format Conversion

Some vendors format `doc_date` as `YYYYMMDD` (no separators). When no `/` character is present in the date field, convert: `YYYYMMDD → MM/DD/YYYY`.

### Currency Sign Removal

Apply to every monetary value extracted on a statement (`inv_amt`, `open_amt`, and any total/aging figures read for validation):

1. Remove the `$` symbol.
2. Remove thousands-separator commas.
3. Keep the decimal point and two decimal digits.
4. Output as a number, not a string.

| Raw | Cleaned |
|---|---|
| `$28.12` | `28.12` |
| `$1,234.56` | `1234.56` |
| `$0.00` | `0.00` |

This mirrors the general CSV data-cleaning rule in GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §3.5 — restated here because statement amounts are frequently read from PDF tables, not just flat files.

### Invoice Number Cleanup — Leading `INV` Prefix

After extracting `invoice_no` (whether from a dedicated column or parsed out of a description like `Invoice #INVC13631`), strip a leading `INV` prefix, case-insensitively, if present:

| Raw | Cleaned |
|---|---|
| `INVC13631` | `C13631` |
| `INV13631` | `13631` |
| `invc13631` | `c13631` |
| `R3412131` | `R3412131` *(no leading INV — unchanged)* |
| `R3INV412131` | `R3INV412131` *(INV not at the start — unchanged)* |

Only a match at the very start of the value counts. Apply this cleanup last, after any parsing needed to isolate the invoice number from surrounding text.

### Supplier Account Number Propagation

Some vendors print the account number only on the first row of a table. When `supplier_account_no` is blank on subsequent rows but populated on the first row, carry the first row's value forward to all subsequent rows.

### Field Swap — Vendors That Print Account in Name Field

A small group of vendors print the EspriGas account number in the `Account_name` field and the display name in a `temp_name` field. When this pattern is detected:
- Copy `Account_name` value → `supplier_account_no`
- Copy `temp_name` value → `Account_name`

### MACCARB — Remove Open_Amt Column

MACCARB statements include an `Open_Amt` column that should not be extracted. Remove all cells with label `Open_Amt` from all tables before processing.

---

## Vendor Reference

### Lampton Welding Supply (Statement)
- **EspriGas Account:** C081784, Branch 000WIC
- **Statement format:** Account-level summary. May be bundled on page 2 of the same PDF as a Rental Invoice (e.g., billing01_C081784_c_...pdf). Treat page 2 as a Statement document.
- **File billing01_C081844_s_...pdf:** Standalone Statement — no associated Rental Invoice in this collection.

### Geer Gas Corporation (Statement)
- **EspriGas Account:** SOUTHW, Branch 000002
- **Statement format:** Account-level summary. Bundled on page 2 of the same PDF as a Rental Invoice (Rent Statement Split.pdf). Treat page 2 as a Statement document.

### Sidney Lee Welding Supply (SIDNEYLEE)
- **EspriGas Account:** TMRES
- **File billing01_TMRES_c_...:** This is a **Statement only** — no individual invoice PDFs are present in this collection. It lists invoice references (content invoice numbers 0000432983 through 0000496175; rental invoice numbers 0010245947 through 0010249652) but the individual invoice PDFs are NOT in this file.
- **Extraction:** No per-invoice line detail can be extracted. Record the header, list the invoice references in `notes`, and mark `extractable: false`.

### MedOx (MEDOX) — "Statement of Account"
- **Statement format:** Header table gives the account number (labeled `Customer`, format `NN-NNNNNNNN-NNNN`) and the customer name (labeled `Customer Name`) side by side — don't confuse the two. Statement date is labeled `As Of`.
- **Transaction table columns:** `TR Date`, `TR Nr`, `SO Nr`, `Site`, `TR`, `Customer PO Number`, `Amount Due`, `Status`, `D`.
- **Column mapping:**

| Target Field | Source Column | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `doc_date` | `TR Date` | Convert to `MM/DD/YYYY` per Date Format Conversion above |
| `invoice_no` | `TR Nr` | Apply the Invoice Number Cleanup rule above (strip a leading `INV`) |
| `inv_amt` | `Amount Due` | Apply Currency Sign Removal above |
| `open_amt` | `Balance` | Only when the layout prints a running "Balance" column (not on the standard MedOx template — seen on other vendors using this same statement style, e.g. CO2Meter.com). Apply Currency Sign Removal. Omit the field entirely when no Balance column exists — do not output a blank value. |

- **Columns to ignore:** `SO Nr`, `Site`, `TR`, `Customer PO Number`, `Status`, `D` — not part of the target schema.
- **Row extraction:** One row per transaction line, in printed order. Stop before the footer disclaimer line (`** IF YOU HAVE ANY QUESTIONS...`) and skip the aging/summary box (`CURRENT / OVER 30 DAYS / ... / BALANCE-DUE`) at the bottom — per the general Sparse Table Removal / Row Filtering rules above, that box is not a transaction row.

---

```json
  "document_type": "supplier_statement",

  "source_rows": ["integer — 1-indexed file line numbers (header = line 1) contributing to this document; omit for PDF/image input (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §3.9)"],

  "rosetta_version": "string (vX.XX — Rosetta Combined version used for this extraction)",
  "confidence": {
    "score": "integer (0–100)",
    "label": "HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW",
    "flags": ["string"]
  },
  "extractable": "boolean",
  "header": {
    "supplier_account_no": "string | null (customer's account number with this vendor; null if not printed anywhere on the statement)",
    "espri_account_no": "string (omit when no override applies — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §14.4)",
    "sold_to": "string (verbatim first line of the Bill To/Customer/Sold To block — see Sold To — Customer Block above)",
    "sold_to_address": {
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string | null",
      "city": "string",
      "state": "string (2-letter code)",
      "zip": "string"
    },
    "statement_date": "string (MM/DD/YYYY)",
    "vendor_name": "string",
    "partner_name": "string (supplier name as printed — same value as vendor_name; populate both, see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §2)",
    "supplier_name": "string (vendor's remit-to entity name — omit entirely with supplier_address when neither a remit-to block nor a general vendor address is present; see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §19)",
    "supplier_address": {
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string | null",
      "city": "string",
      "state": "string (2-letter code)",
      "zip": "string"
    },
    "trade_partner": "string (see Statement Header Fields — §TP.3 lookup; empty string if no match)",
    "parent_vendor_no": "string (omit entirely if no §TP.3 match — see Statement Header Fields)",
    "comment": "string (text following a literal \"Comment:\" label anywhere on the statement; omit entirely when not present — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §28)"
  },
  "lines": [
    {
      "invoice_no": "string",
      "doc_date": "string (MM/DD/YYYY)",
      "type": "string",
      "inv_amt": "number",
      "open_amt": "number"
    }
  ],
  "notes": "string"
}
]
```

## Confidence Scoring

See `confidence_scoring.md` for the shared scoring model, output format, and application steps.

### Required Header Fields

| Field | Tier | Deduction |
|-------|------|----------:|
| `supplier_account_no` | 1 | −15 |
| `vendor_name` | 1 | −15 |
| `sold_to` | 2 | −10 |
| `statement_date` | 2 | −10 |
| `sold_to_address` | 3 | −5 |

> **Tier 1 fields** also populate `required_fields_missing` when absent and flag the document for manual review — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §15.

### Integrity Checks

| Check | Condition | Deduction |
|-------|-----------|----------:|
| No invoice lines | `extractable = true` but no lines extracted | −20 |
| Invalid statement date | `statement_date` cannot be parsed as a valid date | −10 |

**Note:** When `extractable = false`, the no-invoice-lines check does not apply. Score against header fields only.

### Minor Flags

| Check | Condition | Deduction |
|-------|-----------|----------:|
| Statement date defaulted | `statement_date` was absent and set to today's date | −3 |
