# SOURCE: proof_of_delivery_extraction_v1.22.md
---

# Proof of Delivery (POD) — Extraction Logic
**Version:** 1.23
**Model Target:** claude-sonnet-5-5
**Min Token Estimate:** ~3,200
**Cache Strategy:** explicit
**Last Updated:** 2026-09-23

---

## Purpose

Classifies and captures Proof of Delivery (POD) documents — vendor-issued records that verify a physical delivery was completed. PODs often include handwritten or system-printed cylinder counts and one or more signatures (driver and/or customer) providing human verification of delivery.

**Current status — Header and Line-Item Extraction Active:** Extract both document-level header fields and line items for every classified POD (see Header Extraction Rules, Line Item Extraction Rules, and Output Schema below). PODs never carry pricing of any kind (no unit price, line amount, or invoice total) — do not attempt to extract or derive any of those; there is nothing to find.

**Short-circuit rule:** PODs classified with HIGH confidence (score ≥ 80) are short-circuited — no separate classification pass is required before extraction. Run header and line extraction directly and route the output to the POD Repository (a post-processing step, not part of model-time extraction). If confidence is below HIGH, flag for manual review before routing.

**Multi-document handling:** PODs frequently appear bundled with other document types in the same file (e.g., a Shipping Paper on page 1 followed by a signature page on page 3, or a Delivery Note packaged alongside an invoice). Classify each page independently per GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §7.4. When a POD page is identified within a multi-page file, treat it as a discrete document.

---

## Classification Signals

A page is a POD when it matches **at least two** of the following signals:

### Primary Signals (strong indicators — one is often sufficient)
| Signal | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| Header contains `"DELIVERY NOTE"` | Most common explicit POD header |
| Header contains `"SHIPPING PAPER"` | Used by Nippon Sanso/Matheson and others |
| Header contains `"DELIVERY RECEIPT"` | Less common variant |
| Header contains `"PROOF OF DELIVERY"` | Explicit label — used by General Air and others |
| Header contains `"DELIVERY ORDER"` | Used by AIRGAS — distinct from AIRGAS's invoice format, which uses a different layout entirely (see `content_invoice_extraction.md`) |
| Page contains `"DRIVER'S SIGNATURE"` field | Printed label with signature line or actual signature |
| Page contains `"CUSTOMER'S SIGNATURE"` or `"RECEIVED BY"` field | Recipient acknowledgement |
| Page contains `"Delivered by:"` and `"Received by:"` with timestamp | Electronic signature format (e.g., Matheson digital POD page, or the "Delivery Ticket" platform below) |
| Page contains `"DRIVER:"` and `"RECIPIENT:"` labels with signature boxes | AIRGAS Delivery Order signature block |

### Supporting Signals (use to confirm when primary signals are ambiguous)
| Signal | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| `"DELIVERY NOTE No."` or `"DELIVERY NOTE #"` in header | POD reference number field |
| `"BILL OF LADING NO."` field present | Shipping/delivery reference |
| `"CYLINDERS RET'D"` and `"DEL'D"` columns | Handwritten or printed cylinder exchange counts |
| `"Order #:"` paired with `"Arrival:"` / `"Departure:"` or `"Completed:"` timestamps | "Delivery Ticket" platform header block (see Known POD Formats) |
| `"Total Ships:"` / `"Total Returns:"` or `"TOTAL SHIPPED CYLINDERS:"` / `"TOTAL RETURNED CYLINDERS:"` | Computed cylinder-exchange summary line |
| Page contains `"FILE COPY"` notation | Often printed on physical POD copies |
| No pricing, subtotals, or invoice totals present | PODs show quantities but not billing amounts |

### Exclusion — Do Not Classify as POD
- Pages that are primarily T&C boilerplate, even if they appear at the bottom of a shipping paper — classify those pages separately as T&C if they are a standalone page, or ignore the boilerplate section if it appears as a footer on an otherwise classifiable POD page.
- Pages with a T&C URL reference only (e.g., `"Matheson Terms and Conditions: https://..."`) — this is not a T&C page; do not reclassify.

---

## Known POD Formats

### SYOXSA — "Delivery Note"
- **Header:** `DELIVERY NOTE`
- **Reference field:** `DELIVERY NOTE No.` (e.g., `129989-0`) → `order_no`
- **Cross-reference:** `REFERENCE` field links to internal order number
- **Sold To:** EspriGas (Bill-To)
- **Shipped To:** End customer location
- **Line columns:** GAS CODE, ID NO., DESCRIPTION, HAZARD CLASS, CYLINDERS RET'D (handwritten), CYLINDERS DEL'D (handwritten), VOLUME, PRICE (often blank), U/M, AMOUNT (often blank)
- **Signatures:** DRIVER'S SIGNATURE (handwritten) + CUSTOMER'S SIGNATURE (handwritten) + RECEIVED BY
- **Filename pattern:** `DelvryImage.{order_no}.{sequence}.{page}.pdf`

### Nippon Sanso / Matheson — "Shipping Paper"
- **Header:** `SHIPPING PAPER`
- **Format:** Multi-page. Page 1 = hazmat shipping manifest with line items and handwritten cylinder counts. Page 2 = printed picking/delivery detail. Page 3 = electronic signature confirmation page.
- **Signature page signals:** `Received by: {name}` → `received_by_name`, `@ {date} {time}`, `Delivered by: {driver_name}` → `delivered_by`
- **Cross-reference:** ORDER field (e.g., `0043438354-00`) → `order_no`
- **Note:** Page 3 may include a T&C URL reference — do not reclassify as T&C; the reference is informational only.

### "Delivery Ticket" Platform — Spectrum Gas, American Welding & Gas, nexAir, Holston Gases, and others
A shared delivery-tracking platform used by multiple independent vendors — same field layout and labels regardless of which vendor's letterhead appears at the top. Treat this as one format family, not a per-vendor format.

- **Header block:** `Date:`, `Order #:` (→ `order_no`), `Arrival:` + `Departure:` (or `Completed:` in place of `Departure:`), `Branch:`, `Customer:` (format `{supplier_account_no} - {customer_name}`), `Bill-to:`, `Ship-to:`, `Emailed to:`, `Stop #:` (optional — not printed by every branch), `P/O #:` (→ `customer_po_number`), `Device ID:` (a telematics GUID — informational only, do not extract)
- **Customer field parsing:** Split on the first `" - "` — the leading token is `supplier_account_no`, the remainder is `customer_name`. If the remainder itself contains an EspriGas identifier (e.g., `"ESPRIGAS - BLUEGRASS SURGERY & LASER"`), apply the GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §1 Ship-To Name Identification rule to it as well.
- **Ship-to parsing quirk:** Some branches (observed on nexAir) print a phone number as the first line of the `Ship-to:` block, before the street address. Do not extract a phone-number-shaped first line as `address_1` — treat it as a ship-to phone number (informational, not currently an output field) and take the next line as `address_1`.
- **Line sections:** `* Hardgoods *` (fee/charge lines — item code and qty only, no cylinder detail) and `* Cylinders *` (item code, description, `Volume:`, `Ships:`, `Returns:`, optional `Lot #:` and `Tag ID:` per-unit detail, `Loc:`). A document may have either section alone or both.
- **Cylinder exchange summary:** `Total Ships: X Total Returns: Y` — a vendor-computed total across all cylinder lines. Not currently a header output field; useful as a cross-check that per-line `qty_shipped`/`qty_returned` sum correctly.
- **Notes block:** `* Header Comments *` or `* Notes *` — free text. Simple operational notes (e.g., `"no empty cylinders"`) go in the document-level `notes` field. Some branches (observed on nexAir for pharmacy/medical accounts) print dense regulatory tracking text here instead (DEA/pharmacy license numbers, expiration dates, a `"QP:"` pharmacist name) — this can include a second, unrelated `"BILL TO: {number}"` line embedded in the free text. **Do not confuse this with the real Bill-to block** — the real bill-to/account data comes only from the `Customer:`/`Bill-to:` header fields, never from text inside `* Notes *`.
- **Signature block:** `Received by: {name}` (→ `received_by_name`) optionally followed by `@ {date} {time}`, and `Delivered by: {name}` **or** `Completed by: {name}` (both → `delivered_by`; treat as the same field regardless of label). Treat `na`, `.`, or any other non-name placeholder as absent — omit `received_by_name` rather than recording the placeholder text. A username-style value (e.g., `"Philemon.singleton"`) is still a valid name — pass it through as printed rather than omitting it.
- **Emergency contact:** `Chemtrec #`, `EMERGENCY RESPONSE NUMBER`, or `Emergency Response Telephone number` — not currently an output field; noted here for future reference, not currently extracted.

### General Air — "Proof of Delivery"
- **Header:** `Proof of Delivery` (explicit), `Delivery Ticket {number}` (→ `order_no`), `Delivery Date`, `Order Placed By` (not currently an output field)
- **Products section:** Each product line prints `Ship Qty:`, then **either** `Del Qty:` (cylinder/each-count lines — maps directly to `qty_shipped`) **or** `Del Vol.:` (bulk-by-weight/volume lines, e.g. `LIQUID CO2 BEVERAGE BULK LB`) plus `Ret Qty:`.
  > **PLACEHOLDER — BULK QUANTITY MODEL REVIEW PENDING:** On a bulk line, `Ship Qty` (what left the truck) and `Del Vol.` (net volume actually delivered, after accounting for product already in the customer's tank) are genuinely different numbers — this doesn't fit the simple `qty_shipped`/`qty_returned` pair used elsewhere. Until this is resolved, extract `Ship Qty` as `qty_shipped` and note `Del Vol.` in the line's own free-text `description` rather than discarding it; do not silently pick one number as though it answers both questions.
- **Rush signal:** An `EXPEDITE FEE` line item is a valid `is_rush` signal — check line items for POD `is_rush` the same way GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §23.2 already does for other document types (this was previously listed as unavailable for POD; it is now available since line-item extraction is active).
- **Lot numbers:** `Manufacturer Lot Number` and `{Vendor} Lot Number` are two distinct values — do not conflate them.
- **Signature:** `Signer's Name: {name}` → `received_by_name`.

### AIRGAS — "Delivery Order"
- **Header:** `DELIVERY ORDER` (header title), `DELIVERY ORDER #` (→ `order_no`), `CUST PO #` (→ `customer_po_number`), `SOLD TO: {number}` (→ `supplier_account_no` — this is EspriGas's own account number with Airgas at this location, not the customer's), `SHIP TO: {number}` (ship-to location code — not currently an output field)
- **Line items:** `Qty Ship`, `Container Ship`/`Container Ret` (→ `qty_shipped`/`qty_returned`), `Cust.Part#` (→ strong `esprigas_item_no` cross-reference candidate — Airgas's own customer part numbers have been observed to already match EspriGas's `esprigas_item_no` digit-scheme format exactly, e.g. `211040`, `111020`, `311010`; treat a `Cust.Part#` match as a confident Step 3 cross-reference hit)
- **Page 2/3 (electronic signature page):** `DRIVER: {name}` → `delivered_by`, `RECIPIENT: {name}` → `received_by_name`, `Completed at: {timestamp}`, `TOTAL SHIPPED CYLINDERS:` / `TOTAL RETURNED CYLINDERS:` summary, `DELIVERY LOCATION: LAT: / LONG:` (GPS coordinates — not currently an output field, but worth a manual glance if delivery location ever needs verification against the address on file)
- **Per-line order/ship/return detail:** `ORD QTY:`, `SHIPPED:`, `RETURNED:`, `BACKORDERED:`. Extract `SHIPPED`/`RETURNED` as `qty_shipped`/`qty_returned` as normal.
  > **PLACEHOLDER — BACKORDER FLAG REVIEW PENDING:** A document has been observed where `ORD QTY` and `SHIPPED` disagree (a real shortfall) while `BACKORDERED` is printed as `NO`. Extract the fields as printed — do not attempt to reconcile or override `BACKORDERED` based on the quantity mismatch; flag the discrepancy for manual review instead if asked to validate consistency.

---

## Account Selection — Multiple Candidates

When account number resolution is required and a lookup returns multiple candidates, apply the standard selection logic:

| Scenario | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Exactly one candidate has `Account Status = Primary` | Select that account number automatically |
| No Primary candidates; exactly one candidate has `Account Status = Backup` | Select that Backup account number automatically |
| No Primary candidates; two or more candidates have `Account Status = Backup` | Flag for **manual review** |

> **Data availability note:** The account candidate database is not yet available. Until then, treat all unresolved multi-candidate account numbers as requiring manual review.

---

## Header Extraction Rules

Extract the following document-level fields from every classified POD, and line items per Line Item Extraction Rules below. PODs never carry pricing — do not extract or derive `invoice_no`, `invoice_date`, `invoice_total`, or any per-line price/amount. If a POD is ever found alongside genuine invoice data on the same page, that page is not a POD — reclassify per GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §7.4.

| Output Field | Source Field | Notes |
|-------------|-------------|-------|
| `partner_name` | Vendor letterhead or document header | Supplier name as printed on the document, extracted verbatim per GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §2. |
| `supplier_name` / `supplier_address` | Remit-to block, or vendor letterhead address as fallback | See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §19. Omit both entirely when neither a remit-to block nor a general vendor address appears on the document. |
| `order_no` | `Order #:`, `DELIVERY ORDER #`, `DELIVERY NOTE No.`, `Delivery Ticket {number}`, or equivalent primary document reference | Tier 1 — see Confidence Scoring. The single canonical identifier for this delivery event, regardless of which label the vendor prints. When a vendor prints multiple reference numbers (e.g. AIRGAS's Delivery Order #/Sales Order/Shipment #), use the one that identifies this specific delivery document — see Known POD Formats for the per-vendor pick. |
| `delivery_date` | Delivery date field | MM/DD/YYYY. Tier 1 — see Confidence Scoring. |
| `customer_po_number` | `P/O #:`, `CUST PO #`, or equivalent | Apply GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §13.10 BC PO normalization after extraction. Exempt from any deduction when absent — many deliveries don't reference a customer PO at all. |
| `trade_partner` | Derived from `partner_name` | BC trade partner code — look up `partner_name` in the Trade Partner Reference table (§TP.2). If found and not listed in §TP.1, use the mapped code. If listed in §TP.1, or if no match is found, output `INSTANTLRN`. |
| `is_rush` | Header fields **and** line items | Boolean — `true` when an expedite signal (`RUSH`, `EXPEDITE`, `EXPEDITED`, `HOT SHOT`; plus `STAT` in header fields only) appears in a header field, **or** when a line item resolves to an expedite fee (e.g. General Air's `EXPEDITE FEE` line) — full line-item signal checking per GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §23.2 now applies, since POD line-item extraction is active. **Excluded:** `Delivery Same Day Emergency Room` (`910061`) is a destination, not an expedite. Output unquoted `true`/`false`. Always populated. No deduction. |
| `delivered_by` | Ship-via → route → `DELIVERED BY` / `CARRIER` / `DRIVER` / `Delivered by:` / `Completed by:` field | Carrier or delivering party, **UPPERCASED** (GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §23.3). Treat `Delivered by:`, `Completed by:`, and `DRIVER:` as the same field regardless of label. **Omit entirely when no carrier is named** — no deduction. |
| `received_by_name` | `Received by:`, `RECIPIENT:`, or `Signer's Name:` field | The name of the person who signed for / received the delivery. **Omit entirely** when the field is blank or holds a non-name placeholder (`na`, `.`, or similar) — do not record the placeholder text. A username-style value (e.g. `Philemon.singleton`) is still a valid name — pass it through as printed. No deduction either way. |
| `supplier_account_no` | Account / Customer number field | Apply the Account Selection — Multiple Candidates logic above if the document yields more than one candidate. |
| `customer_name` | Ship-To or Received By name block. If this block identifies the account using an EspriGas identifier (per GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §1), apply the Ship-To Name Identification / Ship-To Exclusion Rule from §1 — see the EspriGas Direct Delivery Integrity Check below | |
| `delivery_address` | Ship-To address block | Split into `address_1`, `address_2`, `city`, `state`, `zip`. Tier 3 — see Confidence Scoring. See the "Delivery Ticket" platform note above for the phone-number-in-address-block quirk. |
| `comment` | Text following a literal `Comment:` label anywhere on the document | See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §28. Omit entirely when no `Comment:` label is present. |

---

## Line Item Extraction Rules

Apply GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §13.3 `item_no` normalization pipeline (ChangeAbbreviation → remove spaces → truncation; no content/rental-specific Step 3 applies here). `description` is extracted as printed; leave blank if absent — do not fabricate one from the item code.

**`unit`:** Normalize to `"EA"` for cylinder/each-count lines, same as Content Invoice (GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md — Content Invoice Line Fields). Bulk-by-weight/volume lines (e.g. General Air's `LIQUID CO2 BEVERAGE BULK LB`) keep their printed unit.

**`qty` / `qty_shipped`:** The quantity shipped/delivered (`Ships:`, `Qty Ship`, `SHIPPED:`, `Del Qty:`). `qty_shipped_provenance` is `"stated"` whenever a shipped quantity is printed for the line (always the case for POD line items — there is no default-quantity scenario here).

**`qty_returned` — never assume an even exchange.** This is the one place POD line extraction differs meaningfully from Content Invoice:
- A `Returns:`, `Ret Qty:`, or `RETURNED:` value **explicitly printed on the line** (including an explicit `0`) → use that value, `qty_returned_provenance: "stated"`.
- **No such field printed for that line at all** → `qty_returned: 0`, `qty_returned_provenance: "not_applicable"`. Do **not** default to `qty_shipped` — POD never applies the Content/Rental "assumed even exchange" fallback, and no flag or deduction applies to this condition either way.
- Hardgoods/fee lines (delivery charges, surcharges, hazmat fees — anything without a cylinder/gas product) always get `qty_returned: 0`, `qty_returned_provenance: "not_applicable"`, same as the equivalent Content Invoice rule.

**`esprigas_item_no` — cross-reference only, no scheme construction.** Apply GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §13.4 Steps 1–3 only (Fee/Resource Mapping, Bulk Gas Product Mapping, Cross-Reference Lookup). **Do not proceed to Step 4 (§13.8 scheme construction)** — the digit scheme's Type digit (position 3) only has defined values for Content (`1`), Rent (`2`), and Cylinder Purchase (`3`); a POD is none of these, so there is no valid Type digit to build with. If Steps 1–3 don't resolve a code, omit the `esprigas_item_no` key entirely — do not write `"NOT IDENTIFIED"` (same policy as Content/Propane/Rental/PO — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §13.4 Step 5). AIRGAS's `Cust.Part#` is a strong Step 3 cross-reference source when present — see Known POD Formats.

---

## Output Schema

**Output format:** Always return a JSON array — one element per extracted document. See GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §16.

```json
[
{
  "document_type": "proof_of_delivery",
  "source_file_output_total": "integer — total output records expected from this source file (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §7.9)",
  "source_page_start": "integer — 1-indexed page number where this document begins in the source PDF/image; omit for CSV/flat-file input (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §7.10)",
  "source_rows": ["integer — 1-indexed file line numbers (header = line 1) contributing to this document; omit for PDF/image input (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §3.9)"],
  "required_fields_missing": ["string — Tier 1 field names absent from source document; omit this field entirely when all Tier 1 fields are present (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §15)"],
  "rosetta_version": "string (vX.XX — Rosetta Combined version used for this extraction)",
  "confidence": {
    "score": "integer (0–100)",
    "label": "HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW",
    "flags": ["string"]
  },
  "header": {
    "partner_name": "string (supplier name as printed, see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §2)",
    "supplier_name": "string (vendor's remit-to entity name — omit entirely with supplier_address when neither a remit-to block nor a general vendor address is present; see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §19)",
    "supplier_address": {
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string | null",
      "city": "string",
      "state": "string (2-letter code)",
      "zip": "string"
    },
    "order_no": "string",
    "delivery_date": "string (MM/DD/YYYY)",
    "customer_po_number": "string (omit entirely when absent — no deduction; apply GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §13.10 normalization)",
    "trade_partner": "string",
    "is_rush": "boolean — true when an expedite signal is present in a header field or a line item; otherwise false (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §23.2)",
    "delivered_by": "string — carrier/delivering party, UPPERCASED; omit entirely when no carrier is named (see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §23.3)",
    "received_by_name": "string (name of the person who signed for/received the delivery; omit entirely when blank or a non-name placeholder)",
    "supplier_account_no": "string",
    "customer_name": "string",
    "delivery_address": {
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string | null",
      "city": "string",
      "state": "string (2-letter code)",
      "zip": "string"
    },
    "comment": "string (text following a literal \"Comment:\" label anywhere on the document; omit entirely when not present — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §28)"
  },
  "lines": [
    {
      "item_no": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "qty": "number",
      "unit": "string (normalized to \"EA\" except bulk-by-weight/volume lines, which keep their printed unit)",
      "qty_shipped": "number",
      "qty_shipped_provenance": "stated",
      "qty_returned": "integer",
      "qty_returned_provenance": "stated | not_applicable",
      "esprigas_item_no": "string (omit this key entirely if unresolved — cross-reference/fee-table lookup only, never scheme-constructed; see Line Item Extraction Rules above)",
      "xref_source": "null (reserved for future cross-reference source tracking; always output null)"
    }
  ],
  "notes": "string | null"
}
]
```

---

## Confidence Scoring

See `confidence_scoring.md` for the shared scoring model, output format, and application steps.

### Required Header Fields

| Field | Tier | Deduction |
|-------|------|----------:|
| `order_no` | 1 | −20 |
| `partner_name` | 1 | −15 |
| `delivery_date` | 2 | −10 |
| `customer_name` | 2 | −10 |
| `delivery_address` | 3 | −5 |

> **Tier 1 fields** also populate `required_fields_missing` when absent and flag the document for manual review — see GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §15.
>
> **No fields related to invoice number, invoice date, or any pricing (including invoice total) appear in this scoring table** — none of that data exists on a POD, so there is nothing to score. Do not add deductions for those concepts on this document type.

### Integrity Checks

| Check | Condition | Deduction |
|-------|-----------|----------:|
| Invalid delivery date | `delivery_date` cannot be parsed as a valid date | −10 |
| EspriGas direct delivery — customer unresolved | Ship-To Exclusion Rule applied (GOVERNANCE_RUNTIME.md §1) to `customer_name` — no non-EspriGas/TMG customer name could be determined — flag `"(-20) esprigas_direct_delivery — non-EspriGas/TMG customer name could not be determined — manual review required"`. **Does not apply** when Ship-To Name Identification successfully resolved `customer_name` by stripping an EspriGas identifier — that is a correct extraction, not a defect, and carries no deduction. | −20 |

### Minor Flags

| Check | Condition | Deduction |
|-------|-----------|----------:|
| `supplier_account_no` absent | Account number not present on document | −3 |

> **No flag or deduction applies** when a line's `qty_returned` defaults to `0` because no Returns field was printed, and none applies when `received_by_name` is omitted because the signature was blank or a placeholder — both are expected, normal conditions for this document type, not defects.

---

# SOURCE: terms_conditions_exclusion_v1.4.md
---

# Non-Extractable Document Types — Exclusion Logic
**Version:** 1.4
**Model Target:** claude-sonnet-5-5
**Min Token Estimate:** ~1,350
**Cache Strategy:** explicit
**Last Updated:** 2026-06-03

---

## Purpose

Identifies document types that contain no transactional data requiring extraction or BC import. All classifications in this file share the same output behavior: **discard with no extraction output**. Two types are currently defined: Terms & Conditions pages and Finance Charge / Late Fee Notices.

**T&C pages are a discard classification.** When a page is confirmed as T&C with HIGH confidence (score ≥ 80), stop processing it immediately — no extraction pass, no archival, no repository routing. If confidence is below HIGH, flag for manual review rather than discarding automatically.

---

## Classification Signals

A page is T&C when it is **primarily composed of legal boilerplate** and matches several of the following signals. No single signal is definitive — evaluate the overall character of the page.

### Strong Signals
| Signal | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| Majority of page text is continuous legal prose (not tabular data) | Key distinguishing characteristic |
| Contains phrases like `"TERMS AND CONDITIONS"`, `"TERMS OF SALE"`, `"CONDITIONS OF SALE"` as a section heading | Explicit T&C header |
| Contains legal clauses: `"LIABILITY"`, `"INDEMNIFICATION"`, `"GOVERNING LAW"`, `"LIMITATION OF LIABILITY"`, `"DISPUTE RESOLUTION"`, `"ARBITRATION"` | Standard T&C clause language |
| Contains `"ALL SALES ARE SUBJECT TO"` followed by legal text | Common T&C preamble |
| Contains `"WARRANTIES"`, `"DISCLAIMER"`, `"AS IS"` in legal context | Warranty disclaimer language |
| No invoice number, PO number, account number, or dollar amounts present | Absence of transactional fields |

### Supporting Signals
| Signal | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| `"REVERSE SIDE"` reference on a preceding page | Common on physical documents where T&C print on the back |
| Page is titled `"IMPORTANT NOTICES"` or `"LEGAL NOTICES"` | |
| Page consists entirely of dense small-print text with no tables or structured fields | Visual pattern of boilerplate |

---

## Important Distinctions — Do NOT Classify as T&C

The following are **not** T&C pages and must not be excluded:

| Scenario | Correct Classification |
|----------|----------------------|
| A T&C URL reference appears as one line at the bottom of a POD or Shipping Paper (e.g., `"Matheson Terms and Conditions: https://..."`) | POD — the URL reference is informational; the page is not a T&C page |
| T&C boilerplate appears as a footer paragraph at the bottom of an invoice or shipping paper alongside transactional data | Classify the page by its primary document type; ignore the footer text |
| A page contains a brief legal notice (1–3 sentences) alongside a signature block | POD or other document type — brief notices do not constitute a T&C page |

**Rule:** A page is only classified as T&C if the T&C content is the **primary and dominant** content of the page. Incidental legal language on an otherwise classifiable document does not change that document's classification.

---

## Output

T&C pages produce **no output**. When a T&C page is identified:

1. Record the page as excluded in any processing log.
2. Do not produce a JSON record or extraction output.
3. Continue to the next page.

If an entire file consists only of T&C pages, record the file as fully excluded with a note.

---

## Finance Charge / Late Fee Notice (`finance_charge_notice`)

A standalone document whose entire content is finance charges, late payment fees, past-due interest, or similar financing-related charges. These carry no extractable product or service data and are discarded in the same manner as T&C pages.

**This classification covers two document patterns — treat identically:**
- Finance charge invoices (document header or all line items indicate finance/interest charges only)
- Late fee only notices (document exists solely to bill a late payment fee)

### Classification Signals

A document is a `finance_charge_notice` when it matches the primary signal AND at least one supporting signal.

**Primary signal (required):**
| Signal | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| All line items are finance charges, late fees, past-due charges, or interest — no product, gas, or delivery lines present | Core distinguishing characteristic |

**Supporting signals:**
| Signal | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| Document header contains `"FINANCE CHARGE"`, `"LATE FEE"`, `"LATE PAYMENT"`, `"PAST DUE NOTICE"`, or `"INTEREST INVOICE"` | Explicit label |
| Invoice total equals the sum of only finance/late fee line items | No product revenue present |
| No item numbers referencing gas products, cylinders, or standard fee codes (delivery, fuel surcharge, hazmat) | Absence of normal content |

### Important Distinction — Do NOT Classify as `finance_charge_notice`

| Scenario | Correct Classification |
|----------|----------------------|
| An otherwise normal content or rental invoice that contains one or more late fee line items alongside product lines | Classify by primary document type; apply the late fee line item rule in `content_invoice_extraction.md` |

### Output

`finance_charge_notice` documents produce **no output**. Apply the same discard behavior as T&C pages:

1. Record the document as excluded in any processing log.
2. Do not produce a JSON record or extraction output.
3. Continue to the next document in the file.
